## Finding your way 

Check out our [Festival Maps page](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/info/maps/) to help you find your way around.

## Camping for the season 

Camping on-site for the full six days of the Woodford Folk Festival is by far the best way to immerse yourself in all the festival has to offer. Not keen on camping? No problem! There are plenty of other accommodation options nearby — [check them out here.](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/prepare/accommodation/) 

## Camping overnight 

Overnight Camping is available on-site, with shower and toilet facilities, plus a Café for all your basic supplies. Your overnight camping ticket gives you access to the Festival Site from 8am on the day of your ticket, but please note that re-entry into the festival precinct the following morning is not permitted. 

Overnight campers need to leave the camping areas by 10am. If you’d like to extend your stay, additional tickets are available at the Overnight Ticket Office located at the Happy Campers tent and open daily from 28th December to 1st January, between 7am and 2pm. 

## Accessibility camping 

We are committed to providing an inclusive and accessible experience for all our patrons. We offer a range of services to support your needs, including accessible camping and amenities, sunflower lanyards, and a buggy transport service to help you get around with ease. Our accessible buses, medication storage facilities, and allowance for assistance animals ensure that everyone can enjoy their visit comfortably. We also provide Companion Card tickets, Auslan-interpreted performances, and a dedicated access support team ready to assist you throughout your experience. We are here to make your time with us as enjoyable and accessible as possible. 

For more information about our Accessible Camping Area please see the [accessibility page.](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/prepare/accessibility/)  

## General Store 

Our General Store is fully stocked with all the essentials (and things you may have forgot). If you’re arriving early for Season Camping on December 26th the General Store opens at 7am, and the Festival Precinct opens at 5pm — so you’ve got plenty of time to get settled before the festivities begin. 

## Overnight Camping Cafe 

There is a Cafe in the Overnight Camping area open from 7.30am to 11.00pm from the December 27th January to 1st. 

## Where can I find ATMs? 

ATMs, which accept most foreign cards and AMEX, are located throughout the precinct-see map for locations. There are no traveller’s cheque facilities available on site. 

## Things to consider when preparing to camp at the festival 

### Facilities 

While we continue to improve the facilities, please remember that our camping grounds are used only a few times a year. Toilet and shower facilities are adequately basic. Peak times for shower queues are in the mornings and later afternoons so please avoid these times if you don’t want to wait. 

### Campgrounds 

Because of limited use it is not possible for us to provide perfectly level camp sites with well-manicured lawns. Several thousand trees have been planted in the camping grounds over the past few years, but they are mostly too small to provide good shade just yet. 

### Weather 

The festival is conducted in the full glory of summer. Our weather can range from very hot and dusty days through to impressive summer thunderstorms. FYI – it gets pretty chilly if you’re still wandering about enjoying The Pineapple Lounge at four in the morning so come prepared for whatever the weather may bring. 

### Water 

Water is always a precious commodity at Woodford as we are self-sufficient and take all our water from on-site tanks. We would appreciate if all festivilians would join with us in conserving water in the following ways: restrict yourself to one shower a day, turn the water off when brushing your teeth and please bring some water with you. Those are the basics. There will be information posted around the campground and the camp warden’s office will be open until late for any queries. 

### Your campsite 

Remember that you are creating a temporary home at your camp. It may be a welcomed retreat from the festivities as well as a place to crash at the end of the day, so please make sure you are comfortable and consider your camping gear carefully. 

## Suggestions for a comfortable campsite 

### Consider the water course 

When choosing a campsite consider where the water will naturally flow in the event of rain and pitch your tent accordingly. 

### Raise your bedding off the ground 

A fold-up camp stretcher allows air circulation and protects your bedding from any water that may enter your tent. Keeping your personal belongings off the ground is also a good idea – a fold-up chair makes a great wardrobe or table. 

### Standing room 

Be able to stand inside your tent if possible or have a tarp stretched somewhere for a comfortable covered area. 

### Bring your own water 

All tap water on-site is potable but for conservation and your own convenience please bring all the water you’ll need for the duration. 

### Power 

Powered Sites are available in the Season Campgrounds for Season with Camping ticket holders only. Powered Sites are an optional add-on to your season with camping ticket.  

Power is also available for patron’s campsites who require it for life-support equipment (accessibility camping area). If you require power for life-support equipment, please head over to our [accessibility page](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/prepare/accessibility/) to complete a request through our accessibility camping form. 

### No generators permitted in the campgrounds 

Please note that use of generators in the camp grounds is not permitted due to noise and pollution concerns. 

### Conserve space where possible 

Our campgrounds need to accommodate a large number of people so please keep your campsites small and conserve space wherever possible. 

### One car per campsite 

Please only keep one car per campsite in the campgrounds. Other cars should be parked at Eastern Bloc Long-term and Day parking area. _Please do not drive around the campgrounds once you have set-up your campsite._ 

### Keep your valuables safe 

Theft can be a problem at any large event, so please do not bring anything of value to the festival other than what is absolutely necessary. _All valuables remain the responsibility of the camper._ 

### Expect noise, bring earplugs 

Campsites near the festival entrance and in other areas hear music from the festival precinct until the late hours of the night and fellow campers may be up and about all day and night. Please bring your ear plugs if you are a light sleeper. 

### Dump point 

There is no dump point located on site, the closest is located at the Woodford Showgrounds, 5 min up the road. 

**PLEASE NOTE: Absolutely no fires, glass or animals are allowed in the campgrounds or on the festival site.** 

_And MOST importantly_ _– We look forward to seeing you at Woodfordia this year for a fantastic festival experience!_

# About Woodford Folk Festival

[Home](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/) • About Woodford Folk Festival

On this page

*   [Building the village](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/about/#building-the-village)
*   [Experience](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/about/#the-programme)

The Woodford Folk Festival is held annually over six days and six nights, from Dec 27th through to January 1st. More than 2,000 local, national and international, artists, musicians and presenters grace the stages of Woodfordia. 

The festival begins each year with the iconic Opening Ceremony and closes with the spectacular showcase, on New Year’s Day. This year will be the 39th Woodford Folk Festival and the 32nd held at Woodfordia. 

It is the largest gathering of artists and musicians in Australia.

The Woodford festival experience is deep, rich and colourful. It is based on a vision of inclusive and creative community, culture and tradition passed through generations, expressed through story and ceremony. The site, a former barren dairy farm, has been lovingly regenerated with over 140,000 subtropical rain forest trees, orchids, ferns and sedges, planted to create a habitat for butterflies and wildlife.

## Building the village

Over the festival, Woodfordia is transformed into a village that hosts over 25,000 daily patrons, performers, stallholders, volunteers and organisers. As many as 2,680 volunteers across 162 departments are at the heart of the organisation and contribute to the setup and day-to-day running of the festival. **During the event, the festival is actually the 67th largest town in Australia.**

Each year construction begins in early December and continues up until Christmas Day. Nearly 1000 volunteers and contractors build the village. Many come from around the world to be part of the festival build, enjoy the festivities, and then stay for a week after to pull it all down. 

![](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/woodford-about-page-1.jpeg)

## Experience

The festival programme features concerts, dances, street theatre, writers’ panels, film festival, comedy sessions, acoustic jams, social dialogue and debate, folk medicine, an entire children’s festival, an environmental programme featuring talks, debates and films, art and craft workshops, circus performances and workshops, late night cabarets, parades and special events.

The festival streets are lined with restaurants, cafes, stalls, bars, street theatre and parades. Tree-filled campgrounds, butterfly walks, ponds and wildlife complete the picturesque site. The festival appeals to a diverse audience with all ages and many nationalities attracted each year. It’s a magical experience, and one not to be missed.

![](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/amphitheatre-woodford-folk-festival_preview-1024x679.jpeg)

## **Woodford Folk Festival media accreditation terms & conditions**

**A limited number of media accreditations are approved each year.**

We really appreciate support given in helping us get the word out about our festival and preference will be given to those who are supporting and promoting Woodford Folk Festival in the lead-up to the event.

**The two types of Media Accreditation available:**

1.  **Media accreditation with event ticketing**
    *   Reserved for members of the press (print, radio, TV, film, news agencies and online media) who represent a significant media organisation, or
    *   Freelancers assigned by a recognised media organisation who meet all other media requirements.
2.  **Media accreditation without event ticketing**
    *   Freelance journalist / photographers on submission and acceptance of project proposal and subject to all other media requirements, or
    *   Photographers working with artists or presenters may apply for specific accreditation, which will be limited to working with the artist or presenter in their programmed venues only.

##  M**edia Accreditation Terms and Conditions** 

**Accreditation will be assessed upon the following:​**

1.  Completed accreditation application.
2.  Applicant/s agree to Media Accreditation conditions and Festival conditions of entry.
3.  Outline of commitment to any available pre-festival coverage in the lead up to the Woodford Folk Festival between mid-October (when our programme is launched) through to 1 Jan (end of event).
4.  Outline of commitment to coverage during and/or post event.

A completed accreditation application must be received prior to the event.   Each outlet may apply for a MAXIMUM of two (2) representatives – _due to request volume, only one representative may be approved._ 

Media passes are provided for ONE day of the event only – unless otherwise negotiated.

**Applications are open through November 2025 and should be submitted by 1 December 2025.**

**Notification of acceptance or otherwise will be provided by 5 December, if not earlier.**

Media passes are strictly personal and non-transferable. If changes to the person accredited need to be made, please contact the Media Dept to organise.

The chiefs of staff of major newspapers and television channels covering the festival on a day by day and changing staff basis are asked to contact the festival Media Dept pre-event or the Festival Media Centre during the event for short notice site visits, so that appropriate arrangements can be made for news crews (i.e. access, parking closest to site for company vehicle).

Festival entry procedures and Media Accreditation check in information will be sent with Media Accreditation acceptance. All accredited media teams entering site must follow entry procedures.

All approved applicants must check in at the **Media Centre** once on site**.** On **presentation of photo identification,** you will be allocated your media accreditation. Accreditation must always be worn and displayed.

Media and photographers are not permitted in backstage areas unless escorted by a member of the Media team. Under no circumstances should media personnel walk through the backstage area. Should this occur or should media/photographers not follow directions of festival staff/security, we reserve the right to immediately cancel accreditation and revoke all festival access.

Media accredited photographers are permitted access to the area close to front main stages but must be always aware of the crowd activity and security. **Use of flash is not permitted when photographing artists on stage.**

Security and WFF staff instructions must always be adhered to.

The media liaison team will inform media and photographers of any other requirements or restrictions regarding artist performances.

Media and photographers must follow the conditions of entry to the festival as well as adhere to the Woodford Folk Festival Health and Safety Policy.

Commercial use of any images and/or footage taken at Woodford Folk Festival requires express permission in writing by the Media Manager.

We ask that you are considerate of these requirements, as they form conditions of your accreditation which may be revoked in the event of a breach. A serious failure to follow these requirements may result in removal from site (and removal of your wristband/ticket).

The Woodford Folk Festival is produced by Woodfordia Ltd. a not-for profit community arts organisation and is supported by the Queensland Government through Arts Queensland and Tourism and Events Queensland.

Located in the Moreton Bay region, the Woodford Folk Festival takes place in a rural valley surrounded by natural bushland with plenty of native wildlife and a superb view of the Glass House Mountains from the hill-top above the festival grounds. The festival is about an hour and a half drive north of Brisbane, or 40 minutes west of Caloundra or an hour south of Noosa. 

[Locate Woodfordia via Google Maps](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/links/wff-google-maps.html)

## Bike

We are currently working on one less car for this years festival

### Why cycle to Woodfordia?

Next year cycle instead.

The joys of cycling are many and various, especially when the ride is along quiet roads through scenic country and the destination is the Woodford Folk Festival. It’s a healthy, non-polluting and relaxing way of getting here.

The two-wheeled alternative becomes easier with a little help from Festival organisers. The Festival offers a free luggage service for Brisbane – based patrons with a Season ticket. You simply need to drop off luggage at the shop of our partners, _Epic Cycles_, in the week before the Festival and we’ll have it ready and waiting at the Festival when you arrive, then return it usually on 2nd January.

Bookings are essential for this service, and can be made through _Epic Cycles_. They’re at **81 Baroona Road, Paddington**, phone **07 3368 2324**. (We recommend them for all matters related to the noble bicycle.)

With luggage looked after, the ride to Woodfordia then becomes an easy undertaking for anyone with reasonable levels of fitness, especially if using the train/bicycle combination. The train – bicycles are free – will get you to stations on the Nambour line north of Caboolture. Trains run about every two hours or less on Boxing Day, which is when most cycling patrons reach the Festival. Check the [Translink website for details](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/links/translink.html) but be aware that the line is often closed at this time of the year for track maintenance, and travellers need to use replacement buses. (They do have luggage compartments for bicycles.)

Once at the Festival – cyclists receive priority if there’s a queue at the Ticketing area – cycling patrons can camp at _One Less Car Camping_. It’s close to the Welcome Gate, is a dedicated camping space for non-motoring Festivilians, and has a marquee for secure bicycle parking, luggage storage and socialising.

We encourage safe and responsible cycling. Please be very visible and sun safe, stay hydrated, carry tools for repairs. Ensure your bicycle is safe and legal: take it to _Epic Cycles_ if in doubt.

It’s more fun, as well as safer, if you have a riding partner. If on Facebook, find _OneLessCar@Woodfordia_ and ask to join the group and you can soon connect for cycling company.

### Which way to go?

All roads to Woodfordia from the train line need to cross the watershed between the Stanley River and the coastal streams. So no matter which way you go, there is an uphill stretch either easy or arduous, depending on your route. Generally the uphill bits are less of an issue on the return journey.

Numbers in brackets after place names refer to distance from starting point.

#### Route 1: from Beerwah station – the popular route

If using _Strava_, the mobile app or website for online cycling routes, [see this page](https://www.strava.com/activities/811368954/share/facebook).

From the train station, turn right, then almost immediately turn left and head west along the Peachester Road. If children are riding with you, you can use the footpath on the right side of the road, it continues well past the Beerwah State School. The road itself has light to moderate traffic. After about six kilometres, the climb begins. It’s not a steep gradient, the road runs through bushland and is well shaded, it twists and turns a fair bit so that traffic maintains a low speed. Towards the top of the climb there’s a break in the vegetation and it’s worth stopping to take in the view of the Glasshouse Mountains to the south – good photo op. You’ll soon arrive at Peachester (9) where there’s a café, picnic table and toilets.

At Peachester you can continue along the main road and face a further climb (and an exhilarating descent) but our route instead turns left onto Commissioners Flat Road. From here the remainder of the route to Woodfordia is especially idyllic, running through bushland and farmland with very little traffic. The road is narrow however, and requires the usual caution. It gradually descends into the Stanley River valley. Soon, you’ll come to a junction where you turn left into Cove Road (17). You can continue straight on for a few hundred metres to rejoin the main Kilcoy-Beerwah Road to avoid two short unsealed sections of Cove Road. The favoured route though is along Cove Road. The unsealed sections total less than three kilometres, traffic is extremely light, and gradually views of the Conondale Range appear over the Stanley River valley. Continue along Cove Road, ignoring several turnoffs (the last of which is Old Cove Road, a pleasant back road which leads to Woodford township). Cove Road then crosses the Stanley River and quickly ends on the Kilcoy-Beerwah Road. Carefully cross the main road here to reach Woodrow Road, follow this for less than a kilometre and you’ll have reached Woodfordia (27.5).

#### Route 2: from Beerburrum station – the most traffic-free

This route is a little shorter, and has much less traffic, than Ride 1. Much of it is through State Forest and about half is unsealed, fairly well graded but after a dry spell it can be quite dusty. Take care if visibility is reduced. Not recommended for narrow-tyred road bikes.

From Beerburrum Station, head out west to the Beerburrum Road, turn left, then after a short distance, turn right onto the Beerburrum-Woodford Road (.54). The route to Woodford is straightforward from here – it runs to the south of Mt Beerburrum, becomes gravel after several kilometres, and continues through pine plantation with some bushland before a short section of sealed road over the watershed. The climb is shorter but significantly steeper than Ride 1. After the climb there’s a major turnoff to the right, the Glasshouse-Woodford Road, but just continue without deviation. There are glimpses of Mt Beerwah through the pines.

Continue west until you reach Golf Course Road (18.54), follow this then turn into George Street which leads straight to Woodford township (20). Then turn right along the D’Aguilar Highway. To avoid the traffic, just stay on the footpath for a little while, follow Durunder Street running parallel with the highway, until you reach Old Cove Road (21) and turn right here. There’s little traffic on Old Cove Road, you may see the Woodfordia sign at the base of the Conondale Range, and the spire-like shape of Mt Beerwah to the east. After a few very easy kilometres, there’s the junction with Cove Road, where you turn left, cross the Stanley River and quickly reach the Kilcoy-Beerwah Road. Carefully cross the main road here, ride up Woodrow Road, follow this for less than a kilometre and you’ll have reached Woodfordia (26).

#### Route 3: from Glasshouse Mountains station – best for mountain viewing

This route has a fine outlook on many of the peaks which make up the Glasshouse Mountains, and is a little longer than Ride 2. From the train station, ride west along Coonowrin Road, then turn left along Old Gympie Road and continue until reaching the Glasshouse-Woodford Road. Traffic so far is fairly light. Follow the Glasshouse-Woodford Road until the road starts climbing steeply towards the watershed and you reach the Glasshouse Mts Lookout (9). It’s worth stopping here to take in the view. The road now becomes unsealed and traffic is very light. Continue until reaching the junction with the Beerburrum-Woodford Road, turn right here and follow directions as outlined in Ride 2 to reach Woodfordia (28).

#### Route 4: from Glasshouse Mountains station – for mountain bikes

The Beerburrum West State Forest is riddled with tracks set up for forestry operations, and is something of a Mecca for SUVs and trail bike riders. None of the tracks are signed, some are eroded beyond belief, and there are occasionally burnt-out vehicles and illegal rubbish dumps. Mobile coverage is unlikely, and paper maps are unobtainable. Google Maps shows a complicated network of tracks, which don’t always coincide with the reality. The ride is better than this preamble would suggest, but you will need a compass for the most direct route through the State Forest.

Starting from the Glasshouse Mts station, ride west along Coonowrin Road, turn left along Old Gympie Road, then very soon turn right into Mt Beerwah Road. There are great views of Mt Coonowrin as you cycle along. The road climbs up towards the watershed and the Mt Beerwah car park (10). There’s a picnic area here and a short walking track to the base of the mountain and the start of the summit climb. If you can resist this adventure, continue west along the Mt Beerwah Road which quickly deteriorates. The sealed road becomes unsealed, and then practically unrideable with massive vehicle-sized potholes. (This could be great fun if you enjoy MTB stunts, but immensely difficult if you’re loaded with luggage). This horror stretch continues for a few hundred metres until the road becomes less steep. The next obstacle is inundation, with ankle deep muddy water covering the entire width of the track (even after several rain-free months). This occurs in several spots before conditions become more comfortable, and the track is fairly flat, running through very pleasant bushland. There are many tracks leading off the route, but the key is to refer constantly to your compass, and head due west without deviation. After possibly ten kilometres from the Mt Beerwah carpark, there is a barbed wire gate with a wild dog poison warning sign – cross through here, then a second gate (don’t forget to close these gates) and a few metres further on, Cove Road. See Ride 1 for directions to Woodfordia from here.

#### Route 5: from Caboolture station – for a fast ride

For cyclists in a hurry this is perhaps the quickest option. Trains to Caboolture are more frequent than to stations further north. The route follows the D’Aguilar Highway, which can be busy unless you make a very early start. While the road shoulder is generous in places, it’s not always so. Watch out for B-Doubles travelling to or from the quarry at Bracalba (17). The significant climb is just past Bracalba and, on the return trip, provides an exhilarating descent. This route is best suited for road cyclists who don’t mind a bit of traffic on the road to Woodfordia (31).

### Touring options

Woodfordia is close to two mountain ranges containing National Parks – Conondale and D’Aguilar – and accessible from two major river valleys – the Brisbane and the Mary. There is also the Brisbane Valley Rail Trail. This all makes for excellent bicycle touring. With a decent map of South East Queensland, you can tailor a multi-day ride to avoid the busy roads and make the most of the scenic wonders seen on the way to Woodfordia.

## Car

### Why not carpool this year?

Instead of loading yourself and a mate into the car, think how many extra seats you have in your car and if any of your friends need a lift. Take one car instead of two! Why increase the amount of cars on the road, parking congestion and pollution at the festival? Offer your friends a lift, split the petrol bill and head for the hills!

Why not use our new [Car Pool Search Page](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/prepare/getting-here/car-pooling.html) thanks to [coseats.com](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/links/coseats.html)?

This sites is free and help put people in contact with others who want to save money and the environment by sharing their travelling costs.

### Driving from south

Drive along the Bruce Highway from Brisbane. Take Exit 152B to Kilcoy (NOT 152A towards Caboolture). Follow the D’Aguilar Highway for approx. 21km. Travel straight through to Woodford. Four kilometres after Woodford, turn right onto Kilcoy-Beerwah Road. Travel one kilometre then turn left into Woodrow Road.

### Driving from north

Turn off the Bruce Highway at Highway 85 (Kilcoy), just short of the Caboolture turnoff, and follow the D’Aguilar Highway to Woodford. Travel four kilometres after Woodford and turn right towards Beerwah, travel one kilometre, then turn left into Woodrow Road.

### Private transfer

Private transfer are available and can be pre-booked. Up to 7 people plus luggage, with prices from around $2 per kilometre. That’s around $150 from Brisbane to Woodford, or Woodford to Sunshine Coast. There are a number of providers in this space. We recommend www.AlbatrossTransfers.com (online booking form) or call Cliff on 0429 959 756

**Be careful of cyclists on the road** 

## Car pooling

At Woodfordia, we believe there is more than driving alone to the festival. We encourage those of you who prefer to come by car, to do it as a group.

To help you, we decided to team up with [bushride.com](https://bushride.com/) – a free website that will help you find the perfect riding match for your journey. You’ll also be able to access it through our app.

Through [bushride](https://bushride.com/), you’ll be able to offer a ride if you’re driving, or a request a ride if you’re a passenger. There are several reasons to choose to carpool:

*   Financial – by sharing the cost of the ride.
*   Environmental – by reducing the number of cars on the road and the number of cars on site, and therefore reducing carbon emissions and congestion.
*   Societal – by developing new friendships.

There is no limit to carpooling. You can choose to travel with your friends and family, but also with fellow Woodfordians. Whether you travel locally or from interstate, there will always be someone making the same journey. So why not share it?

Enjoy your travels and please do not hesitate to share them with us through our [Facebook page](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/links/onelesscar.html) or by email: [onelesscar@woodfordia.com](mailto:onelesscar@woodfordia.com).

Travel safe!

## Air

Fly into Brisbane airport and catch the airport train to Eagle Junction. Then catch the Caboolture train, and get off at Caboolture Station. There are connecting buses from here to the Festival at various times.

See [Getting here by public transport](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/prepare/getting-here/by-public-transport.html) for more details on transport options to the Festival from Caboolture.

We are proud to offer a supported and inclusive experience for all Festival patrons ensuring that everyone can enjoy the magic of Woodford. The following will provide you information on what we offer.

Our team are here to help make your Festival experience as enjoyable and accessible as possible.

Please take a moment to explore the below information and if you have any questions, please reach out to our friendly team in the office on [07 5496 1066](tel:+61754961066) during office hours, 9am–5pm AEST Monday to Friday.

If you need assistance completing your accessibility application form, please call us so we can complete it on your behalf.

## Accessibility services

*   Buggy transport
    
*   Accessible buses with wheelchair lifts/ramps
    
*   Accessible campgrounds
    
*   CPAP zone camping
    
*   Accessible amenities
    
*   Support team services
    
*   Cold medication storage (First Aid Tent)
    
*   Reserved accessible seating in venues and wheelchair viewing platform
    
*   Charging for mobility devices and medical equipment
    
*   Accessible site maps available from Infology and Access Support office
    
*   Assistance animals (by application)
    
*   Hidden Disability Sunflower lanyards
    
*   Auslan interpreted performances
    
*   Communication boards for non-verbal patrons
    
*   Air-conditioned sensory room
    
*   Wristband exemptions for patrons with sensory needs
    
*   Wheelchair accessible bar counters (La Grande & Piano Bars)
    
*   Access support information desk at Infology
    
*   Companion Card tickets (by application)
    
*   Accessible camping (by application)
    
*   Sharps bins
    

## Accessible camping

**Accessible Camping Applications Close at 5:00PM 4 DECEMBER**

Our Accessible Camping area is located close to the Festival entrance and is designed to support ease of movement and comfort. The campground features accessible amenities, flat and stable surfaces, and a dedicated Access Support Tent within the campground. Our team is on hand to assist and help ensure a safe, comfortable, and enjoyable stay throughout the Festival.

Our team will start assessing applications mid-year. Our team will email you the outcome of our application or call to discuss your application further if necessary.

Please complete the below form to apply for an Accessible Camping spot.

If you are bringing along an assistance animal, please ensure you also complete the assistance animal application form below.

_**Please note:** Space is limited, so ensure you get your application in early. We are unable to accept applications after the cut-off date._

\***_Before completing the Accessible Camping form, please ensure you have first purchased your tickets to the Festival (as the form will request your booking confirmation number)_**

[Apply for accessible camping](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/forms/accessible-camping)

## Tent City

Accessible patrons who wish to hire a tent through Tent City and have it set up in the Accessible Campgrounds must first purchase a festival ticket that includes camping. You will then need to apply for accessible camping using the form above and indicate in your application that you plan to book with Tent City.

Once your accessible camping application has been submitted, please contact Tent City directly to arrange your tent hire and advise them that you will be staying in the festival’s Accessible Campgrounds.

Our Access Support team will then liaise with Tent City to coordinate the setup of your tent within the accessible camping area.

Book your accomodation with Tent City [HERE.](https://tentcityhire.com.au/woodford-folk-festival1/)

## Powered Sites

Powered Sites are available to accessible campers who require power for medical reasons.

For patrons who require power for CPAP machines only, with no other mobility needs, you will be camped in our CPAP Camping Area behind Glamping Tents 19–20 in the Season Campgrounds and not in the Accessible Camping Area.

CPAP camping powered sites are 6mx6m, if you require a larger campsite, please purchase a Powered Site Add-on ticket.

All other accessible campers that require power with additional needs will be located in the Accessible Camping Area.

_**Please note:** All patrons accessing power are required to bring a 25m extension lead that has been tested and tagged before arrival._

All powered sites are subject to an additional payment to cover the cost of the powered site. This will be processed over the phone when your application for a powered site is approved by our team.

## Day visitors

Day visitors who require accessibility parking may park in the reserved accessible parking space directly across from the Transit Lounge on the Eastern Bloc. Please collect your Day Accessibility Parking pass from the Solutions Tent to display on your windscreen. If you already hold a disability parking permit, you may park in this area without the need for a festival issued accessibility parking pass.

Day visitors who require parking close to the Festival entrance and use mobility devices that exceed the capacity of our accessible bus lift are encouraged to contact our Access Support team so we can assist with making suitable arrangements.

If you are bringing along an assistance animal, please ensure you also complete the assistance animal application form below.

Access Support Services for day visitors can be found at the Infology tent in the Festival precinct.

## Assistance animals

We welcome Assistance Animals and require you to register your Assistance Animal prior to your arrival. To help us support you and your Assistance Animal, please complete the form below.

Assistance Animals must be registered, trained and wear an identifying coat or collar, and be kept on a lead at all times whilst attending.

Patrons with Assistance Animals must also apply to camp in the Accessible Camping area.

[Register an assistance animal](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/forms/assistance-animal)

## Companion card tickets

We are proud to be affiliated with the Australian Companion Card Scheme, offering valid companion card holders a complimentary Festival ticket. Complete the form to apply for your complimentary ticket.

Please ensure the person who requires a companion has purchased their Festival ticket first.

Applications after 22 DEC may proceed directly to the Solutions Tent and show their Companion Card to receive their ticket on the day.

[Apply for a Companion Card ticket](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/forms/companion-card)

## Sensory space

Our Sensory Space offers a quiet, low-stimulus environment for patrons who may feel affected by noise, crowds, overwhelm, or fatigue, or who simply need a calm break from the Festival.

Located in an air-conditioned building next to the Festival Ears and First Aid tent, this space is designed to support rest and regulation, providing a gentle place to recharge before returning to the festivities.

## Auslan interpreted performances

Auslan interpreters will interpret selected performances at the Festival. Look for the “interpreted” symbol in the printed and online programme.

You can also book a performance to be Auslan interpreted through the Auslan service at the Festival. This phone number is in the programme book and available from the Access Support Team.

Reserved Auslan seating will be available at all interpreted performances.

## Transport services

### Accessible shuttles

Accessible shuttles fitted with ramps and lifts operate 24 hours per day moving patrons from the Eastern Bloc car park – Overnight Campgrounds – Festival Entrance and Season Campgrounds.

### Opening and closing ceremony shuttles

Accessible shuttles to and from the Opening and Closing Ceremonies can be booked directly via Access Support Services, located in the Access Support Office in Season Campgrounds and Infology Access Support desk.

### Buggy transport

Buggy services are available during the Festival for pick-up and drop-off around the precinct. There are five designated buggy stop locations throughout the Festival site. Bookings can be made directly through Access Support Services, either at the Access Support Office in the Season Campgrounds or at the Infology Access Support desk.

## Accessibility map

Accessible maps will be available for collection from the Access Support Office and Infology.

Venue maps highlighting reserved accessible and Auslan seating areas will also be displayed at the Access Support Office and Infology.

_\*The below map is from the 2025/26 Festival and is subject to change._

[](https://woodfordfolkfestival.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/25-Acc-buggy-A5-map-scaled.jpg)

_Click the image to enlarge._

## Amenities

We have a number of conveniently located accessible amenities in the season accessible campgrounds and throughout the Festival precinct.

These amenities are marked on the Festival maps in the programme, website and on maps that can be collected from the Access Support office and Infology Tent.

There are also a number of amenities that have medical sharps bins.

## Hidden disability sunflower lanyards

Woodfordia recognises that not all disabilities are visible. We offer complimentary Hidden Disability Sunflower Lanyards that are available for collection from the following locations:

*   **Solutions Tent (Eastern Bloc)**
*   **Access Support Office (Season Campgrounds)**
*   **Infology**

## Mobility scooters

Mobility scooters are permitted within the Festival precinct.

On arrival, please collect a Mobility Scooter Pass from the Welcome Gate team or the Access Support team. For the safety of all patrons, mobility scooters must operate at a strict maximum speed of **5km/h** within the precinct.

_Please note that e-scooters and e-bikes are not permitted within the Festival precinct and are not considered mobility devices._

## Medical services

### Festival Medical Centre

The medical centre is located behind the General Store in the season camping area. Open for first aid 24 hours a day from 2pm on the 25th of Dec until Midday on the 2nd of Jan.

### First Aid

In addition to the Medical Centre a First Aid post is located next to the Festival Police Station, opposite the Chai Tent – open 9am to 1am.

### Essential medications storage

Limited cold storage of medications will be available if required. Should you require this service, please visit the Festival Medical Centre, behind the General Store.

### Ambulance

There will be first aid, paramedical and emergency medical personnel on-site 24/7 during the event.

### Emergency hotline

In the case of an emergency, please call the hotline number on your wristband. **07 5496 1033**

## About our Festival site

While we’ve made significant efforts to provide accessible facilities and services across the Festival, Woodfordia is a natural, rural site and this brings some unique conditions. At times, the ground can be dusty or muddy, and some areas may be uneven or gently sloped.

Over the years, we’ve continued to improve pathways throughout the site, including many upgraded access routes. However, some pathways remain dirt or gravel. The Festival site is expansive, with the entertainment precinct alone covering approximately 50 acres, so we encourage patrons to plan ahead and allow time to move comfortably between areas.

## Contact us

We’re here to support people with disabilities to plan a safe, comfortable, and inclusive festival experience.

If you’d like more information or assistance with accessible camping, parking, or site access at the Woodford Folk Festival, please contact our reception team at [reception@woodfordia.com](mailto:reception@woodfordia.com) or call [07 5496 1066](tel:+61754961066), Monday to Friday, 9am–5pm (AEST).

##### Where The Gallery Meets The Street

### Get to Know Us

Darwin Street Art Festival is based in the unique tropical city of Darwin, on Larrakia land in the Northern Territory. This place is home to a creatively rich and diverse community of artists whose work has enlivened our streets and enriched our lives since 2017.  
The Festival has been a catalyst for public arts and community, bringing local, national and international artists together to share their work in public spaces for all to enjoy. Over this time, the Festival has found a place in the hearts of locals and visitors who value the creative energy it has brought to Darwin.

​

DSAF is delivered by Proper Creative, run by David Collins who has a strong background in the rich history of graffiti and street art in Darwin and the NT. The festival is funded by the Northern Territory Government, and supported by many other valued sponsors.

​

​Since its inception in 2017 DSAF has transformed the streets of Darwin into a spectacular outdoor art gallery that attracts thousands of visitors each year.

CONV ACTIVATING ABANDONED SPACES / PANEL TALK ![Ticketed event](/assets/adw/ticketed-event-star.svg) 12pm - 2pm

Add to calendar [Apple / OutlookApple / Outlook](https://adelaidedesignweek.com.au/program/activating-abandoned-spaces-panel-talk.ics) [Google — Sun 18 Oct, 12pm - 2pmGoogle — Sun 18 Oct, 12pm - 2pm](https://adelaidedesignweek.com.au/program/activating-abandoned-spaces-panel-talk/google-calendar/0)

This panel discussion investigates the cultural, social, and aesthetic potential of abandoned and underutilised urban spaces in Adelaide. It begins by questioning the notion of abandonment itself: in what sense are places abandoned, by whom, and according to whose values? Far from being neutral, abandonment is a political and value-laden condition that reflects changing patterns of ownership, economic priorities, and public attention. Rather than viewing abandoned spaces as sites of failure or decay, this project explores how art, design, and aesthetic engagement can reveal the qualities already embedded within them. Such spaces offer opportunities to acknowledge loss, embrace ambiguity, and discover new forms of meaning and connection. They can become environments where cultural experimentation, informal occupation, and community activity emerge beyond the constraints of commercial productivity. This panel conversation will explore how undefined urban spaces are essential for social transformation and civic self-organisation. In a market-driven city, spaces that exist outside commercial exchange can provide rare opportunities for collective authorship and public life. Through design interventions, community engagement, and creative occupation, we ask whether Adelaide can reclaim overlooked urban spaces and transform them into places of social, cultural, and civic potential (can we create our own version of Federation Square?), whether at a metropolitan scale or through a network of smaller, everyday interventions. Join us for a discussion that leads into the Shop Front Design Tour from 2-5pm, and AWD closing drinks at Honey Dripper.

### Contributors

*   Contemporary curator Chloe Tanner (Tasmania) sits in conversation with public artist Julia Townsend, architect Dr Richard Le Messurier and artist/designer Tom Borgas. Moderator: Chloe Tanner Chloe Tanner, an independent contemporary art curator, lives in nipaluna/Hobart, Tasmania. Her work is informed by her upbringing in the Amazon jungle, the ultimate abandoned environmental frontier. She works between Europe and Australia. Her thesis, ‘The Art of Abandonment’, explores the psychogeography of abandoned places. Panelists: Julia Townsend, Dr Richard Le Messurier and Tom Borgas. Julia Townsend is an Adelaide-based artist whose practice explores the relationship between abstraction, architecture and public space. Working across large-scale murals, painting and site-responsive projects, her work investigates how abstract forms can transform the experience of built environments and create new ways of engaging with place. Drawing inspiration from architecture, construction processes and urban landscapes, Townsend's work considers how visual interventions can activate spaces, encourage public interaction and contribute to the cultural identity of cities. Through both permanent and temporary works, she is interested in the capacity of art to reveal new possibilities within overlooked, transitional and underutilised environments. Her practice examines themes of transformation, adaptation and renewal, with a particular interest in the creative potential that emerges when spaces become undefined or exist between established uses. By introducing abstraction into architectural contexts, her work invites audiences to imagine alternative ways of experiencing the built environment and encourages a sense of curiosity, play and possibility within the city. Dr Richard Le Messurier is an Adelaide-based design practitioner and lecturer who works across architecture, landscape architecture, and urbanism. Operating under the moniker MEDIUM, his design practice spans multiple scales—from residential additions to urban interventions—with a special interest in the social and behavioural impacts of form. This approach extends from his 'Design as Research' PhD, which examined the impacts of short-life, creative interventions in overlooked and interstitial urban spaces. This interest was informed by his time working with European collectives operating within abandoned public spaces, such as Exyzt Collectif and Guerilla Architects. Richard continues to explore these themes through self-built installations and academic work. Richard argues that untapped public value can be unlocked in Australian cities through the use of creative architectural tools. Yet such approaches have been minimally explored on this continent. His contribution to this issue was recognised when ‘Cultivating Quiet’—a project examining the unrealised Australian suburban front yard—was selected for inclusion in the Unsettling Queenstown ‘Open Archive’ at the Australian Pavilion for the 2023 Venice Biennale. Tom Borgas is a visual artist and educator living and working on the traditional land of the Kaurna people in Adelaide, South Australia. His work explores the politics of images, objects and processes that sit at the intersection of art and architecture. Working predominantly with everyday materials his practice is an experiment in what happens when spaces, people and three-dimensional form come together. Tom has exhibited at shows and galleries around Australia including PICA (Perth), The Jam Factory (Adelaide), Artisan (Brisbane), Salamanca Arts Centre (Hobart), MARS gallery (Melbourne), Stockroom (Kyneton) and as part of the 2018 Kyneton Contemporary Art Triennial. Commissioning bodies and collaborators include: UAP, The City of Brisbane, Rockhampton City Council, Moreland City Council for Melbourne’s Level Crossing Removal Project, Splendour in the Grass, Hilton Hotel Adelaide, The Adelaide Festival Centre, The City of Adelaide, Illuminate, The District Council of Karoonda East Murray, Renewal SA and OSCA. Together with Amber Cronin, Tom is also one half of Fallow, a critical spatial practice that focuses on site-sensitive, immersive experiences that connect and build ecological communities through sculpture, installation, performance and education.

In 1996 he moved to Canberra to study furniture design and fine woodworking at Canberra School of Art under the direction of the late George Ingham. YITPI YARTAPUULTIKU - Soul of Port Adelaide: The Story Behind an Award-Winning Place Discover the remarkable story behind YITPI YARTAPUULTIKU - Soul of Port Adelaide, a multi-award-winning public realm project that has transformed the heart of Port Adelaide. Join Architect Ashley Halliday and Landscape Architect Warwick Keates as they take the audience behind the scenes of the project's conception, design development, and delivery. This engaging presentation explores how architecture, landscape architecture, planning, culture, history, and community aspirations were woven together to create a place of lasting significance. Through insights into the co-design process, working with cultural knowledge, key challenges, and moments of innovation, Ashley and Warwick reveal the thinking that shaped a project now recognised for its design excellence and contribution to public life. Whether you are a design professional, student, or community member, this presentation offers a unique opportunity to understand how thoughtful, place-based design can celebrate identity, strengthen connection, and leave a lasting legacy for future generations. A free event, bookings essential. Presented by the School of Architecture and Built Environment, Adelaide University.

## LUCKY DUMPLING MARKET 2026 IS ON NOW

Popping up in Elder Park on the Adelaide Riverbank, Lucky Dumpling Market is back from Friday 9 October until Sunday 1 November 2026.

Dumplings, noodles, bao, barbecue, curry and more – taste the flavours of Asia at Lucky Dumpling Market, Adelaide’s springtime food and entertainment hub. There’s a wide range of delicious desserts and refreshing drinks too!

**New in 2026: Lucky Dumpling Market will open at 12pm on Fridays, so come down for lunch!**

There’s entertainment on the Lucky Dumpling Market stage Thursday to Sunday, and you can also see OzAsia Festival’s beautiful Moon Lanterns lit up every night the market’s open.

No need to book; this is a non-ticketed event.

Please note that Lucky Dumpling Market is a cashless venue, meaning all purchases need to be made by card.

##### What is Lucky Dumpling Market?

Lucky Dumpling Market has been a popular hub for food, bars and entertainment on the Adelaide Riverbank each Spring since 2017. It is usually held as part of Adelaide Festival Centre’s [OzAsia Festival](https://www.ozasiafestival.com.au/), Australia’s leading international arts festival engaging with Asia.

Lucky Dumpling Market is run by the team behind [Gluttony](https://gluttony.net.au/),  
the Adelaide Fringe venue hub in Rymill Park.

OzAsia Festival is run by Adelaide Festival Centre.

##### When is Lucky Dumpling Market open?

Lucky Dumpling Market’s scheduled dates are Friday 9 October \- Sunday 1 November 2026.

Tuesdays: from 4:30pm  
Wednesdays: from 4:30pm  
Thursdays: from 4:30pm  
Fridays: from 12pm (new opening time!)  
Saturdays: from 12pm  
Sundays: from 12pm

Food vendors finish serving at 10pm Tue-Thu and Sun, and at 11pm Fri-Sat.

Closing times follow the end of food service, though the market may stay open a bit later if it is still busy. This depends on the night of the week, weather conditions, etc. The market will stop entry and become exit-only for a period before closing time, to allow patrons already inside to finish their food and drink before close.

##### Is 2026 the last season of Lucky Dumpling Market?

Thankfully, no! Lucky Dumpling Market will return in 2027, and beyond.

In August 2026, Adelaide Festival Centre announced that this would be the final season of OzAsia Festival. So while this season is your last chance to experience OzAsia Festival, it is not the last you will see of Lucky Dumpling Market.

##### Where is Lucky Dumpling Market located?

Lucky Dumpling Market will pop up in 2026 in [Elder Park](https://explore.cityofadelaide.com.au/business-listings/elder-park/), on the South Bank of Torrens Lake, in the Adelaide Riverbank precinct. Entry is via the riverside pathway on the northern side of Elder Park (near Popeye’s landing), or King William Road on the southern side of the park. In addition to picnic tables, there is lots of lovely grass to sit on, so we encourage you to bring your own picnic blanket and make yourself comfortable to take in the Riverbank views.

##### What are the entry requirements for Lucky Dumpling Market?

Entry to Lucky Dumpling Market is free. Food and beverages are available for purchase by card from the bars and food vendors.

Lucky Dumpling Market is an all-ages event.

No smoking or vaping is permitted in Lucky Dumpling Market.

You do not need to register or book tickets, as it is a non-ticketed event.

##### How can I express my interest in becoming a food vendor at Lucky Dumpling Market?

Applications have closed for this season, check back later for 2027 Expressions of Interest.

##### When are the busiest times for Lucky Dumpling Market?

Our peak time is between 6pm and 8pm, and even busier on Fridays and Saturdays from 5pm until about 9pm. If you would prefer to avoid queues, you could consider visiting us on a midweek (Tue – Thu) evening, for Friday lunch (the market is now opening each Friday at 12pm), or before or after the peak period on weekends. Also, if a particular vendor has a long line, perhaps visit another vendor instead – all the food is excellent inside Lucky Dumpling Market!

##### Are the OzAsia Festival moon lanterns at Lucky Dumpling Market?

For the first time, OzAsia Festival is showcasing its full array of moon lanterns in the Lucky Dumpling Market precinct. Most lanterns will be within the bounds of the market, complemented by, within the River Torrens itself, Kurdany Tangku, created by South Australian artist Jaydenlee Tong and symbolising Rainbow Serpent Dreaming. These lanterns will be on display for the duration of Lucky Dumpling Market’s season, 9 October – 1 November (market closed Mondays).

![](https://luckydumplingmarket.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/LDM26_OzAsia_Moon_Lanterns_Map-1024x724.jpg)

You can also take a stroll to the Riverbank Footbridge to see the spectacular 40-metre Hong Kong Dragon by Vivian Ho, gazing over the festival.

Find out more about Moon Lanterns at Lucky Dumpling Market on the [OzAsia Festival website.](https://ozasia.adelaidefestivalcentre.com.au/whats-on/moon-lanterns-at-lucky-dumpling-market "https://ozasia.adelaidefestivalcentre.com.au/whats-on/moon-lanterns-at-lucky-dumpling-market")

##### Is Lucky Dumpling Market accessible?

Lucky Dumpling Market is an inclusive venue. [Please find our Access and Inclusion statement here](https://luckydumplingmarket.com/lucky-dumpling-market/access-inclusion/).

##### Which food stalls are at Lucky Dumpling Market?

Visit the ‘[Eat and Drink](https://luckydumplingmarket.com/lucky-dumpling-market/eat-and-drink/)’ page for this information.

##### What are the vegan food offerings?

Visit the ‘[Eat and Drink](https://luckydumplingmarket.com/lucky-dumpling-market/eat-and-drink/)’ page for this information.

##### What are the gluten-free food offerings?

Visit the ‘[Eat and Drink](https://luckydumplingmarket.com/lucky-dumpling-market/eat-and-drink/)’ page for this information.

##### What are the drink offerings at Lucky Dumpling Market?

Lucky Dumpling Market features multiple bars, including:

*   Sake Bar, serving sake, Asian spirits, umeshu and Japanese beer
*   Riverside Bar, serving Australian wines, beer, sparkling sake, soft drinks and more
*   Pirate Life Bar, serving beer, cider and pre-mixed spirits and more
*   Coffee and Cocktails Bar, serving coffee, tea, cocktails and more

Non-alcoholic drink options include:

*   Soft drinks and mineral water
*   De-alcoholic beer and wine
*   Coffee
*   Bubble tea
*   Iced Tea
*   Vietnamese iced coffee
*   Juices

There are free water refill stations for patrons to fill up their drink bottles – please bring your own bottle!

##### Does Lucky Dumpling Market operate on a cashless system?

Yes. Since 2018, Lucky Dumpling Market has used a cashless point-of-sale system. This means that all food and beverage purchases need to be made by card.

For those who have no card option, temporary cards can be exchanged for cash at the Lucky Dumpling Market info booth. These cards can be used to purchase food, drinks and merchandise at Lucky Dumpling Market points of sale.

##### What should I bring with me to Lucky Dumpling Market?

*   a debit or credit card, as all food, drink and merchandise purchases must be via EFTPOS
*   a refillable water bottle, to drink from the free water stations
*   a picnic blanket – while there are tables and chairs, these are in high demand at peak times, and there is plenty of grass to sit on
*   sun protection for during the day, eg hats, shirts, sunscreen – while there are multiple shade structures, the large park is in full sun during the day
*   warm layers for the evenings – there is a cool breeze off the river!

##### What entertainment is available at Lucky Dumpling Market?

Lucky Dumpling Market features a stage, on which there are performances and other entertainment, Thursday and Friday evenings, and Saturday and Sunday afternoons and nights. The entertainment program for each week is listed on our What’s On page.

For the first time, in 2026 OzAsia Festival will present its full array of Moon Lanterns within the Lucky Dumpling Market precinct. Find out more on the [OzAsia Festival website](https://ozasia.adelaidefestivalcentre.com.au/whats-on/moon-lanterns-at-lucky-dumpling-market).

##### Who can I contact about entertainment at LDM?

You can express your interest in performing at Lucky Dumpling Market [via this form](https://gluttony.events/LDM26PerformerCallout).

##### Are dogs permitted in Lucky Dumpling Market?

Dogs are welcome in Lucky Dumpling Market, provided they are on a lead, well socialised, and their owners clean up after them. Please bring your own water bowl for your dog to drink from. We recommend dogs stay up until 7pm, after which the market can become busy and noisy for animals.

##### Can I bring my own food and drink into Lucky Dumpling Market?

Patrons are not permitted to bring any alcohol into Lucky Dumpling Market; it is against our liquor licence conditions.

You are permitted bring small amounts of food into Lucky Dumpling Market – although with so many wonderful food options, we encourage you to purchase from our food vendors!

You are invited to bring your own drink bottle and make use of our free water refill stations. Please ask our bar staff if you need help locating water.

##### Is there shelter at Lucky Dumpling Market?

There are shade tents for sun and rain cover, the rotunda, a covered sake bar, and umbrellas over picnic tables. It is an open-air site, so we recommend you prepare for the forecast weather and bring your own sun protection and rain gear.

##### Where is the nearest car parking, including accessible parks and drop-off points?

Lucky Dumpling Market’s location in Elder Park is adjacent to the Adelaide Festival Centre; you can see the parking suggestions [on their website here](https://www.adelaidefestivalcentre.com.au/your-visit/festival-centre). For on-street parking, you can try War Memorial Drive or Victoria Drive. According to the [City of Adelaide website](https://www.cityofadelaide.com.au/transport-parking/parking/accessible-parking/), the nearest accessible car parks are on War Memorial Drive near the northern end of the Riverbank Footbridge, Victoria Drive near Jolley’s Boathouse, and Festival Drive near the Adelaide Festival Centre.

Please note that entry for Lucky Dumpling Market is via the riverbank pathway on the northern side of Elder Park (near Popeye’s landing), or King William Road on the southern side of the park. These gates can be accessed from the following drop-off points:

*   Jolley’s Lane off Victoria Drive. From the end of Jolley’s Lane, take the paved riverbank pathway west, passing under the King William Rd bridge, and staying on the path as it curves north and comes up along the northern edge of Elder Park
*   Festival Drive off Montefiore Rd, near the lift at the southern end of the Riverbank Footbridge. After taking the lift down, you can then travel on the paved switchback path down to the riverbank pathway, then east to reach Lucky Dumpling Market’s entrance.

##### Is there free public transport to Lucky Dumpling Market?

Take advantage of the free City Connector bus, offering a hop-on and hop-off service to the city and North Adelaide linking popular city attractions, shopping, dining and key destinations. Bus route 98A and 98C connect North Adelaide with the city, and 99A and 99C connect the inner-city. Services operate every 15 minutes on weekdays and every 30 minutes on weekends. For timetables, route details and real-time information visit Adelaide Metro.

The Festival Plaza tram stop is close to the King William Road gate of Lucky Dumpling Market. The FESTVL tram line operates on weekends, public holidays and Adelaide Oval event days. Find out more [via Adelaide Metro](https://www.adelaidemetro.com.au/routes/FESTVL).

##### What measures have Lucky Dumpling Market taken towards being environmentally sustainable?

Lucky Dumpling Market strives to be environmentally responsible. All plates, bowls, cutlery and cups are compostable, and wine is served in reusable cups. We have avoided using single-use plastics wherever possible. A three-bin system is in place to separate compostables, recyclables, and general waste. We encourage you to bring in your own drink bottle.

##### Where can I receive updates about Lucky Dumpling Market?

Please follow Lucky Dumpling Market on social media for more updates.

*   [Facebook](http://www.facebook.com/luckydumplingmarket)
*   [Instagram](http://www.instagram.com/luckydumplingmarket)
*   [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@luckydumplingmarket)

You can also [subscribe here](https://gluttony.events/LDMNewsSubscribe) to email updates.

##### HOW CAN I REPORT LOST PROPERTY?

If you have lost property at Lucky Dumpling Market, you can report it and leave your contact details [via this form.](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/Te1FPYhAp8)

##### HOW CAN GET IN TOUCH WITH THE LUCKY DUMPLING MARKET TEAM?

Email info@gluttony.net.au

# Perth Comic Arts Festival is celebrating Ten years in 2027  Comics Manga Graphic Novels Comic Strips Vertical Comics Bande Dessinée Webcomics

](https://pcaf.org.au/about/)

**PCAF** is a not-for-profit organisation created to share love for sequential storytelling with **free, creator-focused events** in Perth, Western Australia.  
We believe **comics are for everybody** and **celebrate comics of all types**, including graphic novels, manga, vertical comics, comic strips and more!

## Read your story for PCAF Stories Kids!

Do you make comics for kids? Would you like to share your comics with a live audience of young comic fans? PCAF Stories is looking for new presenters for Kids PCAF Stories, happening Sunday the 1st of November at the State Library Theatre. If you’re based in WA, or you’ll be in Boorloo for the event, we’d love to see what you make!

[Read More](https://pcaf.org.au/pcaf-stories-callout-nov26/)

![](https://pcaf.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Expressions-of-Interest1-e1789019845535.jpg)

## PCAF Stories Kids: Looking for a FRIEND Edition!

PCAF Stories Kids is BACK, and this year we’re on the hunt for friendship in the wild and wonderful universe of comics! Get ready for big laughs, awesome stories, unexpected surprises and a whole lot of comic-book fun!

[Read More](https://pcaf.org.au/pcaf-stories-kids-looking-for-a-friend-edition/)

![](https://pcaf.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Advertising-FRIEND-Edition-01.jpg)

## 2026 Brussels Comic Residency Awarded to Alicia Rutigliano

PCAF, in association with the Musée de la Bande Dessinée, is very proud to announce that the inaugural WA comics-artist residency in Brussels is awarded to Alicia Rutigliano!

[Read More](https://pcaf.org.au/2026-brussels-comic-residency-awarded-to-alicia-rutigliano/)

![](https://pcaf.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Brussels-Annoucement-1.png)

## Silly Billy Winners (Winnies) Announced

Everyone has waited on bated breath... give it up for our our official Silly Billy winners (aka Silly Billy Winnies) as announced at the PCAF Exhibitors' Afterparty! What are the Silly Billies, I hear you ask? Only the silliest, most trivial, most inconsequential comic awards this side of the equator! Silly categories include “The Best Rendering of a Butt” and “The Sparkliest Anime Eyes”. Nominations were made on Market Day at this year's PCAF to our roving judges.

[Read More](https://pcaf.org.au/2026-silly-billy-winnies/)

![](https://pcaf.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/748845106_1525662239572592_3410707490271700039_n.jpg)

## Read your story for PCAF Stories Kids!

Do you make comics for kids? Would you like to share your comics with a live audience of young comic fans? PCAF Stories is looking for new presenters for Kids PCAF Stories, happening Sunday the 1st of November at the State Library Theatre. If you’re based in WA, or you’ll be in Boorloo for the event, we’d love to see what you make!

[Read More](https://pcaf.org.au/pcaf-stories-callout-nov26/)

![](https://pcaf.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Expressions-of-Interest1-e1789019845535.jpg)

## PCAF Stories Kids: Looking for a FRIEND Edition!

PCAF Stories Kids is BACK, and this year we’re on the hunt for friendship in the wild and wonderful universe of comics! Get ready for big laughs, awesome stories, unexpected surprises and a whole lot of comic-book fun!

[Read More](https://pcaf.org.au/pcaf-stories-kids-looking-for-a-friend-edition/)

![](https://pcaf.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Advertising-FRIEND-Edition-01.jpg)

[More News](https://pcaf.org.au/news/)

## Other Events & Projects

We’ve got a calendar chock-full of comics even _outside_ of our annual festival. Take a look!

[![](https://pcaf.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/P5081534-400x400.jpg)](https://pcaf.org.au/pcaf-stories/)

### [Pcaf stories](https://pcaf.org.au/stories/)

Comic readings held twice a year with events for kids _and_ grown-ups.

[![A person writes on a sticky note laid out to show a comic strip.](https://pcaf.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/325378324_2198934480292873_7595442457061556217_n-400x400.jpg)](https://pcaf.org.au/academymonthlysession/)

### [Pcaf Academy](https://pcaf.org.au/academymonthlysession/)

Monthly free workshops with comic creators sharing their knowledge!

[![](https://pcaf.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/TALETOWN2025web_005.webp)](https://pcaf.org.au/tale-town/)

### [Tale Town](https://pcaf.org.au/tale-town/)

PCAF’s annual free newspaper of comics featuring a ton of indie creators.

[![](https://pcaf.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/PCAF-2025-Sat-157.jpg)](https://pcaf.org.au/exhibitions/)

## Frequently Asked Questions

Got a burning question about PCAF? Check out our FAQ – we might have the answer you’re looking for!

![PCAF 2025 Sat-207](https://pcaf.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/PCAF-2025-Sat-207.jpg "PCAF 2025 Sat-207")

#### General FAQs

Is PCAF Free?

Entry to both days of the festival weekend (Academy Day and Market Day) are always free. Our artist talks, panels, workshops and other activities are also free entry, but may require a booking to manage room capacity. Our free events are often fully booked over the festival weekend, so be sure to get a ticket so you don’t miss out!  
We also run satellite events throughout the year, and these might be paid events – check the event details to make sure!

Is PCAF a Charity/Not-For-Profit?

The Perth Comic Arts Festival is a Not-For-Profit Arts Organisation [registered](https://www.acnc.gov.au/charity/charities/b85decf2-2b71-e911-a981-000d3ad02a61/profile) with the Australian Charities and Not-For-Profits Commission (ACNC). 

Who organises PCAF?

The Perth Comic Arts Festival is made possible by:

**The Organising Committee**, a group of volunteers who are passionate about the comic arts community of WA (you can read more about them [here](https://pcaf.org.au/about#committee));

**Our General Members**, who assist PCAF with matters of governance (many of whom also assist with the running of the festival); 

And our **On-the-day Volunteers**, who help us with ticketing, setting up and packing down the festival, manning the information desk, answering questions, and countless other tasks that need to get done.

How can I help out with PCAF?

Thanks for taking an interest! We’re always looking for more hands on deck.  
There are a bunch of ways to support PCAF – check out the [Get Involved](https://pcaf.org.au/get-involved) page for more information on:

*   Becoming a Volunteer
*   Donating or becoming a Friend of the Festival
*   Sponsoring or Collaborating with PCAF

Other ways you can support PCAF include:

*   Commenting or sharing our posts on social media to help get the word out – we’re on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/perthcomicartsfestival/) and [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/PerthComicArtsFestival)!
*   Displaying a poster or flyer at your workplace
*   [Donating your Containers for Change refund](https://www.containersforchange.com.au/wa/donate-your-refund) to PCAF – our member number is **C11573701!**

Thought of another way to support PCAF? [Email us](https://pcaf.org.au/contact)!

I want to make comics! How do I get started?

Awesome! We recommend coming to our [monthly PCAF Academy](https://pcaf.org.au/academymonthlysession) meetups, where you can meet and learn from other comic creators. You can also join the [Facebook group](https://pcaf.org.au/academymonthlysession/) and ask questions there.

But really, as long as you have drawing tools –– even if that’s just a notebook and a pencil –– that’s all you need! There’s no secret recipe, and sometimes the hardest part is just getting started. Don’t worry about if you’ll be able to do your epic concepts justice, and just get comfortable making comics with whatever ideas come into your head.

Start sketching comics and feel out what works for you, as everyone’s process and goals are different. It’s okay if those first attempts stay in your sketchbooks, but you can also try making short zines out of the ones that feel worth sharing. Many PCAF exhibitors get started that way.

See our [Comics in WA](https://pcaf.org.au/wa-comics/) page for more local inspiration and resources.

What is PCAF's stance on AI?

**Perth Comic Arts Festival denounces all uses of generative artificial intelligence.** PCAF will not knowingly promote AI-generated materials, nor will we allow any such work to be a part of our festival.   
Read our [AI statement here](https://pcaf.org.au/ai-statement/).

#### Market Hall

_For a more detailed FAQ on Market Hall applications, check out the [Market Hall](https://pcaf.org.au/market-hall) page._

Who exhibits at the PCAF Market Hall?

The PCAF Market Hall is a celebration of comics and the creators who make them. The comics on display at the Market Hall range from trade print runs to DIY at home printed works, and we’re open to all different genres of comics as well as creators of all stages, be they hobbyists, students, or professional comic makers. 

Our key requirement is that **comics be the focus of all Market Hall tables.**

While exhibitors are permitted to sell other items such as prints and stickers, if you work is more focused on illustration, fanart, and merchandise, the Market Hall may not be an appropriate event for you, and we recommend checking out our friends at [Tokyo Alley Perth](https://www.tokyoalleyperth.com/) who run events with Artist Alleys of a broader scope.

Why is the PCAF Market Hall mostly half tables?

When visiting the PCAF Market Hall you may notice that the vast majority of exhibitors are allocated a half table, which is a bit different from some other artist alley/market events. Because PCAF is a dedicated comics event, our exhibitors should prioritise comics, ensuring they make up the majority of their stock. While half tables might mean exhibitors are not able to display as much non-comic stock as they may do otherwise at other events, it helps the Market Hall host as many different makers as possible. Do I need a ticket to enter the Market Hall?

Not at all! The Market Hall is free for the public to come and go as they wish. Tickets are only required for events that have a limited capacity, like workshops, talks, etc. 

![Photo: Kis Heiner](https://pcaf.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/WEB-7302-scaled.jpg "WEB-7302")

![](https://pcaf.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/P9240136-scaled.jpg)

#### Ticketing

Where can I get a ticket to your events?

We usually manage ticketing through our [Humanitix page](https://events.humanitix.com/host/perth-comic-arts-festival), but check the event details for specifics!

If an event is free, why do I need a ticket? Can't I just show up?

We often ticket our free events so we can manage the capacity of a venue for health and safety reasons. We also want to make sure everyone who wants to come to our event is able to and can be sure they’ve got a spot waiting for them when they arrive. It also really helps us manage an event when we know what the expected turnout is!   
To avoid disappointment, especially if it’s an event during the festival, we really recommend you get a ticket. If the room is full and you don’t have a ticket, we’ll have to turn you away!

This event is sold out but I really want to come! Can you make space for me?

We recommend adding yourself to the waitlist via Humanitix – this option should show up when tickets are sold out. If someone cancels a ticket, Humanitix will automatically contact people on the waitlist with an opportunity to get a ticket. I got a ticket but I can't come to this event anymore!

We usually set up our tickets on Humanitix to allow self-serve ticket cancellations – [you can find instructions on how to do this here](https://help.humanitix.com/en/articles/8924075-i-want-to-cancel-my-tickets#h_09aa3f2b09). If you’re having trouble cancelling your tickets, get in touch via Humanitix, or email [info@pcaf.org.au](mailto:info@pcaf.org.au). Please cancel your ticket even if the event is free – this frees up your spot so someone else can come!

We strongly encourage you to consider cancelling your ticket if you become unwell – our events are often indoors and can sometimes get quite crowded.  

## Still have a question?

Get in touch via our [Contact page](https://pcaf.org.au/contact) and we’ll see what we can do.
