ES

[EN](https://www.ifema.es/en/about-us/people-talent "Translate to english")

ES

[EN](https://www.ifema.es/en/about-us/people-talent "Translate to english")

     ![Portal de transparencia  institucional](https://www.ifema.es/img/m/portal-transparencia--institucional/info-ifema.jpg)

## Trabaja con nosotros

¡Buscamos a personas como tú! Si quieres trabajar con nosotros entra y descubre cómo puedes hacerlo. Únete a la experiencia IFEMA MADRID, donde podrás crecer como profesional o comenzar tu carrera formándote con nosotros.

[Más información](https://www.ifema.es/contacto/trabaja-con-nosotros)

     ![Equipo humano de Ifema](https://www.ifema.es/img/m/equipo-humano-ifema/image_nosotros_optimized.jpg)

## Así somos: las personas primero

Somos una organización pensada por y para las personas, capaz de entenderlas y ofrecerles el valor que necesitan para desarrollarse profesional y personalmente. En IFEMA MADRID somos un punto de encuentro entre personas que buscan descubrir, compartir y crecer juntas, impulsando el bienestar social, económico y personal.

En IFEMA MADRID apostamos por la evolución constante y el compromiso por estar siempre un paso por delante de quienes nos rodean, para así poder ofrecer una visión de cerca de todo aquello que nos importa. Una fuente de inspiración y oportunidades para aquellos que tienen intereses comunes y encuentran en IFEMA MADRID un espacio en el que compartirlos.

  ![Video Talento](https://www.ifema.es/img/m/video-talento/caratula-talento.jpg)

## Talento joven

Las personas en formación son críticas  para nuestro crecimiento. Sabemos que los jóvenes son fundamentales para el desarrollo y la creatividad y nos apoyamos en ellos para estar a la vanguardia como fuente constante de inspiración.

Si te gusta conectar personas e intereses, si tienes inquietudes, hablas idiomas, convives con la curiosidad, te consideras dinámico, en IFEMA MADRID te ayudamos a convertirte en un gran profesional, acércate: aceleramos tu aprendizaje acompañándote en tu desarrollo.

     ![Todos juntos](https://www.ifema.es/img/m/todos-juntos/image_asi-somos-2_optimized.jpg)

## Nadie es tan bueno como todos juntos

La experiencia nos ha llevado a reconocer la contribución de todas las personas que forman parte de la institución, fundamental en el éxito conjunto. Una de las claves para el intercambio de experiencias y conocimiento entre equipos es la promoción de proyectos que faciliten el encuentro transversal de personas que no colaboran directamente en el día a día. Impulsar equipos diversos favorece una evolución continua en los métodos de trabajo.

     ![Nuestra mejor version](https://www.ifema.es/img/m/nuestra-mejor-version/image_asi-somos-1_optimized.jpg)

## Cada día, nuestra mejor versión

Realizamos un esfuerzo constante para que la mejora continua de nuestra actividad tenga repercusión sobre los diversos públicos que atendemos. El compromiso por mejorar el día a día de nuestros trabajadores nos impulsa ayudándonos a alcanzar el nivel de excelencia que una organización como la nuestra quiere ofrecer a la sociedad.

     ![Diversidad](https://www.ifema.es/img/m/diversidad/image_asi-somos-4_optimized.jpg)

## El valor de la diversidad, está en la inclusión

Para el fomento de una cultura colaborativa exitosa es imprescindible generar entornos e iniciativas que permitan eliminar barreras físicas y culturales entre áreas y equipos favoreciendo la igualdad de oportunidades y el respeto a la diversidad, tratando de erradicar todo tipo de discriminación. Además trabajamos para asegurar que los beneficios de nuestra actividad lleguen a todos los ciudadanos por igual para crear una sociedad más inclusiva que no deje a nadie atrás.

     

## Pequeños equipos, grandes resultados

Las personas son una de las piezas angulares del plan de futuro y parte de nuestra responsabilidad. Ofrecemos oportunidades formativas para todos nuestros trabajadores que generan un entorno dinámico y en continua evolución favoreciendo el desarrollo profesional y personal de cada uno.

     

## Lo que te afecta a ti, nos afecta a todos

Trabajamos a diario para ser el punto de encuentro entre intereses compartidos, entre empresas y sociedad. Para ello, promovemos un entorno laboral flexible que propicie la conciliación de la vida personal y laboral de nuestros empleados, siendo un referente y un ejemplo en este ámbito. Nos preocupa el desarrollo integral de las personas en todas sus dimensiones, por eso apoyamos el voluntariado corporativo y todas las acciones que pontencian el lado más humano.

     

## Conocer la percepción de nuestros clientes para comprender nuestra realidad

Entender a nuestros clientes es fundamental para nosotros, ofrecerle experiencias que le aporten valor, que marquen diferencia y generen interés, es el camino para comprender sus inquietudes. Utilizamos la empatía como eje para escuchar a los clientes y conseguimos  una relación más sana, duradera y bidireccional, donde tanto cliente como empresa resultan beneficiados..

# SANTA CRUZ LONGBOARD UNION

# LogJam

Sat, Apr 27

|

Pleasure Point

Logjam! annually attracts over 100 competitors ranging in age from 7 to 60+, from all over California. Contestants bring their cherished vintage “logs,” pre-1970 longboards weighing 20 lbs or more. They are surfed without a leash; truly a show of classic longboarding!

* * *

Please Contact our Team Captain to Register

[See other events](https://www.santacruzlongboardunion.com/)

## Time & Location

Apr 27, 2024, 7:00 AM – Apr 28, 2024, 7:00 PM

Pleasure Point, Pleasure Point, CA, USA

## About the event

Logjam! annually attracts over 100  competitors ranging in age from 7 to 60+, from all over California.  Contestants bring their cherished vintage “logs,” pre-1970 longboards  weighing 20 lbs or more. They are surfed without a leash; truly a show  of classic longboarding!

## Atelier Qualia Surf

Qualia is a labor of love, a passion for artisanal work and a deep love for the ocean. Born and raised in Fleurines, France just outside of Paris, Fantine Capron, would seem unlikely to become a boardbuilder and Atelier Qualia Surf founder. But as a lil’ French grom, she spent summers visiting family in Laguna Beach. Little did she know, it would be her destiny. From her quaint village in the forests of Picardy, she moved to California permanently in 2018 to realize her childhood dream of surfing everyday of the year.

Benjmark Surfboards

## Benjmark Surfboards

Benjmark Surfboards was founded by Rebecca Benjamin in Santa Cruz, CA. In 2015 Benjamin began working for 2 Mile Surf Shop in Bolinas, CA and it was this job and the love of surfing that would later have Benjamin moving to Santa Cruz in 2018 to finish her degrees in Computational Mathematics and Legal Studies. In 2020 when the pandemic hit and Benjamin was finishing her thesis on the Hydrodynamics of Surfboard Design, 2 Mile Surf Shop burnt to the ground so instead she found herself spending hours at Almar Surf Works learning shaping and resin work from Michel Junod and Jon Henderson (Strive Surfboards). The fusion of mathematics and surfing blend together in Benjamin’s unique perspective of approaching the water and the crafts which she creates.

# Sponsorship & Vendors

## Become a SPONSOR or  
RETAIL/FOOD  
Vendor

The SCLU Memorial Day Club Invitational is the longest-running longboard surf contest in the United States. It’s not just fun for surfers; this community event raises much-needed funds for local nonprofit organizations benefiting our community members.

Join us in supporting local nonprofits and showcasing your support of Santa Cruz surf culture! Sponsors get direct exposure to hundreds of contestants, their families and thousands surfing fans from across the state. [Contact us](https://www.santacruzlongboardunion.com/sponsorship) for more information or [you can fill out our sponsor sheet](https://www.santacruzlongboardunion.com/_files/ugd/0ce5f1_a5dd3ad166dd482bbfccc35d46f34b1b.pdf) an email it to [santacruzlongboardunion@gmail.com](mailto:santacruzlongboardunion@gmail.com?subject=Sponsorhip)

# 2026 Platinum Sponsors

A huge thank you to our platinum sponsors! We are immensely and sincerely appreciative for their contributions to our event and providing us with some [awesome jerseys](https://www.santacruzlongboardunion.com/platinum-sponsors#pacificwavesurfshop), [totes](https://www.santacruzlongboardunion.com/platinum-sponsors#uroko), [internet,](https://www.santacruzlongboardunion.com/platinum-sponsors#cruziointernet) [socks](https://www.santacruzlongboardunion.com/platinum-sponsors#merge4) and place to store our trailer year round.  Please be sure to visit and support our local businesses.

Pacific Wave Surf Shop

## Pacific Wave Surf Shop

Pacific Wave Surf Shop is a family owned business that opened in 1993 on Pacific Avenue, in the heart of downtown Santa Cruz. After the Loma Prieta earthquake changed much of downtown, Pacific Wave was able to move into the empty and damaged old historical building that was once the county bank in 1895. Inspired by other local surf shop, but also by the ever growing surf and skate culture that embodies Santa Cruz, Pacific Wave has taken the local surf shop mentality to a whole new level.

[![PacWave SurfClub](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/0ce5f1_aaa9852c022b48838636d83063d63b86~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_378,h_283,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/PacWave%20SurfClubv2.jpg)](https://pacwave.com/)

Uroko

[![uroko](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/0ce5f1_eada01bcb2044272be274bba779729d3~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_378,h_283,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/uroko_logov4.jpg)](https://uroko.com/)

## Uroko

The Japanese word UROKO means “fish scales”. I thought it was fitting for a small line of clothes that would represent the passion ocean faring people have in their hearts. If you love the sea or the creatures in it, and perhaps at times feel like a sea creature yourself, then I hope you enjoy the art and clothing that I make in celebration of it.

Enjoy!  
Alex Czech

Cruzio Internet

## Cruzio Internet

Cruzio, established in 1989, connects businesses and residences around Santa Cruz County and parts of the Bay Area with multi-gigabit fiber internet, business-grade wireless internet, and other internet and web services. Our beautiful headquarters in downtown Santa Cruz serve as an IXP and data center, with colocation, flexible office space and coworking for startups and small businesses.

[![cruzio](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/0ce5f1_319c2ceabc3044d4b09582c5d13056ce~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_378,h_283,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/cruziov4.png)](https://cruzio.com/)

Unwavering Support

## The Old Wrigley Building

[![Old Wrigley Building.jpeg](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/0ce5f1_eea13a90b7be46e1a32d692950d8a35a~mv2.jpeg/v1/fill/w_378,h_283,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Old%20Wrigley%20Building.jpeg)](https://uroko.com/)

Owned and operated by William Ow. William Ow has been working in commercial real estate for over 20 years, and is a 3rd generation native Californian with deep roots in Santa Cruz. William specializes in leasing, sales and 1031 exchanges. Commercial Real Estate Sales, Leasing & Investment in Santa Cruz CA. Retail - Office - Warehouse - Land - Triple Net - Investments - R&D - Industrial - Flex Space. William owns and operates the University Business Park LLC (former Wrigley Building).

## Merge 4

At MERGE4, we are committed to creating the best socks out there. Our approach is simple - we merge creativity, positivity, performance, and functionality to create socks that look good, have a great hand feel, and last. MERGE4 is also about celebrating individuality. We're not only focused on making socks - we're also doing our part to make the world a better place by always trying to take being socially responsible and sustainable to the next level.

### About art renzei

Art Renzei is a multimedia art festival that ignites artistic curiosity, engages the community, and reinvigorates the Long Beach

Through multimedia and sculptural art, Art Renzei breathes new life into our surroundings. We invite you to go out and see the world differently!

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5efa5725687297122b5bd0ad/baaa2e50-13f2-4de8-86a0-445de2616b3d/Spencer+Little+detail.jpg)

### Presented by creative class collective

Accessible art for all.

Creative Class Collective programs focus on developing creativity through community engagement and positively impacting the lives of creative industry workers. 

Creative Class Collective makes spaces for collaboration, with the belief that connection fuels creation.

Learn more about [Creative Class Collective](https://www.creativeclasscollective.org/).

# SANTA CRUZ LONGBOARD UNION

# Contest  
Information

This event is an Invitational, open to Coalition of Surfing teams ONLY. Contact your team captain for rules and sign-up Information.

​

Team Captains:

To register your teams for our contest, please go to [LiveHeats.com](https://liveheats.com/). Your club’s entries will not be final until payment is received.

​

Camping Information:

We have a limited amount of camping spots this year!!

![Santa Cruz Lighthouse](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/0ce5f1_ebc36da565c146ea90284b25cb59b20b~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_347,h_393,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/0ce5f1_ebc36da565c146ea90284b25cb59b20b~mv2.jpg)

1 

To pay for your registered team competitors

Team captains can pay for registered team competitors via LiveHeats.com. Individual competitors please contact your team captain on how to pay. The cost per competitor for the divisions are as follows:​

​

*   Push In: $50
    
*   Novice: $50
    
*   Menehune: $110
    
*   Junior: $110​
    
*   All Other Divisions: $150
    

2

Camping Reservation

This year we will have a limited number of camping spots near our contest in the parking lot directly across from our vendors. Only car camping will be allowed (no tents).  Team captains please contact Matt Freeman [sclupresident@gmail.com](mailto:sclupresident@gmail.com) for more information.

![IMG\_1196.JPG](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/0ce5f1_19551ba7438c4eac90be8f97a35d4d4c~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_3840,h_278,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/0ce5f1_19551ba7438c4eac90be8f97a35d4d4c~mv2.jpg)

## Get in Touch

If you have more questions about our contest please contact us at: [santacruzlongboardunion@gmail.com](mailto:santacruzlongboardunion@gmail.com?subject=Memorial%20Day%20Contest)

SCLU Union

For more information about club activities please contact us

​

Email:

# 2026 MADE BIKE SHOW EVENT

August 21 @ 9:00 am - August 23 @ 4:00 pm

$13.00 – $49.00

![](https://made.bike/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Screenshot-2026-01-15-at-6.15.48-PM.jpg)

The MADE Handmade Bike Show is an annual event that celebrates the art and craftsmanship of handmade bicycles. It features hundreds of bikes from builders all over the world – more than 200 builders and brands – as well as workshops, demonstrations, films and other events. The show is a great place to learn about the latest trends in bike design and construction and to see some of the most beautiful and unique bikes in the world. Kids are free to enter.

Portland, Oregon August 21 – 22 – 23, 2026 @ Zidell Barge Building

Friday 8/21/26 : (9 am – 5 pm)

Saturday 8/22/26 : (9 am – 5 pm)

Sunday 8/23/26 : (9 am – 4 pm)

# SANTA CRUZ LONGBOARD UNION

# About

Founded 1981, the SCLU is a 501(C)(3) not-for-profit surf club. The SCLU is also a proud member of the [The Coalition of Surfing Clubs (CSC)](http://www.surfclubs.org/), an international organization that represents the interests of surfing clubs throughout California and the world. 

​

Membership to the SCLU is by invitation. To join the club, you must be sponsored by a current member in good standing. Prospective members must attend three club meetings and contribute volunteer hours to the club. Prospective member votes are held quarterly.

[Current Board](https://www.santacruzlongboardunion.com/current-board)

# ABOUT  
SYDNEY  
FRINGE

###### Photography Credit: Clare Hawley

[Sydney Fringe Festival i](https://sydneyfringe.com/)s the largest independent arts festival in New South Wales and a [NSW Foundation Event](https://www.nsw.gov.au/departments-and-agencies/dciths/ministerial-media-releases/committing-to-our-calendar-of-crowd-favourite-events) with over 350 events presented in over 70 venues across Greater Sydney each year.

## VISION

Sydney Fringe has a vision to be celebrated as one of the world’s leading Fringe festivals, and we are well on our way. Each September, emerging artists and culture creators from all over the city join forces with us to share Sydney’s stories, presenting new work across all genres. Outside of festival time, Sydney Fringe works with public and private sector partners to activate unused space, drive policy and regulatory reform, and advocate for independent artists. All in an effort to build a vibrant and sustainable arts, culture and creative industries sector.

We’re also building the organisation itself for the long term. Our 2026–2029 strategic plan amplifies Sydney Fringe from a September festival into a year-round cultural institution with the infrastructure, partnerships and programming to support artists and audiences twelve months of the year. That means new commercial partnerships, deeper philanthropic relationships, and a more diverse, resilient revenue base, all in service of the artists and independent creators who are the reason we exist.

We are a not-for-profit, open-access festival, which means we welcome all artists, creative people and audiences from all walks of life. Each September, culture creators from all over the city join forces with us to demonstrate the kind of city they want to live in all year round. Our program is curated by our artists, for our audiences. Where else can you see hundreds of world premieres made in your own backyard? And if you’re visiting our beautiful city, what better way to get to know Sydney’s true feelings?

The Sydney we love is vibrant, experimental, expressive, playful, creative and diverse. We look forward to a day when our creative communities are adequately resourced, effectively supported and valued for the contribution they make to our great global city. Until then, we’ll keep building toward it by transforming the landscape of our city into unique experiences you won’t find at any other time of the year, and laying the groundwork so that work continues well beyond September.

Join us for the Sydney Fringe Festival every September for a month of delicious, unfiltered, eclectic performances, where literally anything could happen. And stay with us for what comes next.

## DIVERSITY OF VOICE

As an open access festival we facilitate the diverse sharing of narratives. Our commitment lies in upholding our values of Freedom of Expression, Access for All, Community Connection, Integrity, and Unfiltered Excellence throughout our endeavours. Radical inclusion is core to the Fringe Festival movement, a global platform that invites artists and audiences alike to share, engage, hear new perspectives and be part of a larger cultural community.

Our festival serves as a converging point for diverse voices worldwide, offering different perspectives. We aim to foster a secure environment where these voices can resonate and individuals can actively engage. Particularly in today’s increasingly complex global landscape, festivals play a critical role as sanctuaries of cultural discourse, where challenging ideas and differing views can be held.

# Partner with Sydney Fringe

Partner with Sydney Fringe to support thousands of performers, events and venues to realise their creative potential.

Growing each year in footprint and diversity, we are Sydney’s festival. With 89 venues, 460+ events, 3,000+ artists and 103,000+ attendees at our 2025 festival, we collectively contributed over $49.1 million in economic impact to the city. We are a celebration of the amazing work of independent artists, art makers and performers.

Each year we invite audiences to explore undiscovered parts of the city for new experiences and fill every corner of Sydney with fierce, brave, delicious, experimental and extraordinary work. For all sponsorship, marketing and fundraising enquiries For The Sydney Fringe please get in touch with our Partnerships team below.

### SYDNEY FRINGE’S MISSION

**Innovating, re-imagining and invigorating Sydney’s art and theatre landscape.**

“Sydney Fringe works year-round with our partners to open cultural spaces across the city, activating unused buildings, transforming laneways, and giving independent artists somewhere to take risks. Every September, those partnerships come alive as pop-up venues reshape the cityscape and audiences discover parts of Sydney they’ve never seen before. That’s what excites us most, creating a lasting shift in how the city makes room for art.”

_Patrick Kennedy_  
_CEO, Sydney Fringe_

We are so proud to work with our partners to build on the cultural fabric of our city and showcase brands through epic events, activations and exquisite moments.

Interested?

[Get in Touch](mailto:hq@sydneyfringe.com?subject=Partnership%20Enquiry)

## 2025 Partnership Highlights

##### Sideshow at The Rocks

The Rocks (PMNSW) and the NSW Government

Sydney Fringe transformed The Rocks into a month-long precinct of live performance throughout September, anchored by the critically acclaimed _When Night Comes_ and surrounded by free street activations that drew audiences through the iconic laneways and across public spaces they’d normally walk straight past. Local businesses became part of the fabric of the event, with foot traffic, dwell time, and after-dark energy shifting the character of the precinct well beyond the performances themselves.

  
  

##### Fool's Paradise

The Entertainment Quarter & Head First Acrobats

Fool’s Paradise, our Festival Garden built in partnership with The Entertainment Quarter and Head First Acrobats, ran for six weeks of cabaret, comedy, circus and acrobatics, drawing more than 77,000 people into the precinct. Within that, Fringe Kids offered a dedicated two-week season of children’s performance, turning the garden into a daytime family destination before it shifted back to adults-only programming each evening.

  
  

##### Fringeville

Georges River Council

Now in its fourth year with Georges River Council, Fringeville took over Hurstville Plaza for a single night that turned the civic centre into a free outdoor performance precinct. The 2025 edition brought local arts and cultural collectives into the programming alongside Sydney Fringe artists, a model that’s deepened each year as the partnership has grown, and one of the clearest examples of how Fringe activates beyond the inner city.

  
  

##### Feast

Georges River Council & Hurstville Entertainment Centre

Feast, hosted by Chinese-Australian comedian and food writer Jennifer Wong, paired six of Sydney’s funniest performers with a chef for a night of storytelling and Korean cuisine at Hurstville Entertainment Centre. Part stand-up show, part communal dinner, it’s the kind of format that only works in a Fringe context: unexpected, intimate, and impossible to replicate in a conventional venue. Feast was the second of two Georges River Council-supported events in the 2025 program, reflecting a partnership that continues to expand in both scale and ambition.

  
  

##### In The Key of G

George Place

In The Key of G returned to George Place for its second year, once again transforming the building’s grand foyer into a live performance space for an evening of improvised music. Curated by musician and composer Cameron Undy, the program brought professional improvisers together with emerging and amateur musicians for an unrepeatable night of collaboration and live composition. It’s a format built around the venue itself: music made for and shaped by the space it’s performed in.

# About

### Held amongst the trees of Botanic Park/Tainmuntilla, WOMADelaide — the World of Music, Arts & Dance in Adelaide — is one of Australia’s most loved festivals.

### For more than three decades, WOMADelaide has showcased global icons as well as tomorrow’s favourites in music, arts and dance from around the world, across multiple stages over the March long weekend.

### It’s a place where discovery happens naturally, where generations return to share unforgettable moments, and where the exchange between artists and audiences creates something more than a music festival: a celebration of our shared humanity.

# About Us

**flash fox·y** \\‘flash ˈfäk-sē \\ - to flash or send a climb on your first try but to do it with your own style and swagger

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/60dcd6d7fa1dbe2cd786c81b/a02487ad-a245-441a-8ae4-d4370b9cdb63/2022_FFCFNorthConway_Affinityclimb14_%40jennflemm.jpg)

Flash Foxy originated to empower women climbers and offer a virtual space to connect over climbing, being outside together, and building community. The inaugural Women’s Climbing Festival in 2016 helped us establish an alternate climbing space in real life that did not center cisgender men. 

The climbing community is not static and Flash Foxy has adapted over the years to meet the needs of its membership as they grow, change and continue to self-actualize. **Presently, Flash Foxy stands with women and genderqueer climbers** - including trans and gender non-conforming folks - who need a space to pursue their love of the sport without having to deal with historic barriers to access.

_Still not sure if Flash Foxy is for you? Check out our_ [_FAQs._](https://www.flashfoxy.com/faq)

## Our Mission

Our Mission is to provide accessible resources, opportunities and welcoming spaces for our climbing community through events and education programs. Originally created to celebrate women climbing with women, our community has grown to include a range of gender expressions and gender identities amongst our membership and leadership teams.

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/60dcd6d7fa1dbe2cd786c81b/94c8ff36-6ca6-487c-b489-50f731f0d114/climbing+rope.png)

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/60dcd6d7fa1dbe2cd786c81b/a389e02f-9552-406b-9336-b768252e8e5a/2026_FFCFBishop_FRIDAY+MEETUPS_catlikeacat-1.jpg)

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/60dcd6d7fa1dbe2cd786c81b/4649f871-0caa-4025-b8c8-d6c232992dd6/2026_FFCFBishop_MULTIPITCH+MAGIC_catlikeacat-13.jpg)

## Our Vision

Flash Foxy is committed to uplifting all community members that disrupt normalcy and need a space to connect away from narratives that tell them they don’t belong. We will continue to build sustainable spaces for women and genderqueer folks and use climbing as a means for change. We hold the belief that no one is “self-made” and therefore Flash Foxy is committed to being in conversation with other anti-oppressive organizations to disseminate knowledge and power, work collaboratively and normalize being transparent in the outdoors industry.

If you want to climb and work on building intentional community, this can be a space for you and your voice to matter, to be present, seen and heard.

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/60dcd6d7fa1dbe2cd786c81b/abe876e0-87da-469a-963b-aa8f66ecfb3e/mammoth.png)

# About Sierra Buttes Trail Stewardship

### Our mission is building sustainable recreation-based communities through stewardship, job creation and world-class events, and providing quality outdoor experiences through trail construction and maintenance in the Lost Sierra.

# We couldn't verify the security of your connection.

## Access to this content has been restricted. Contact your internet service provider for help.

[_Video Production by Drop Media_](https://www.dropmedia.tv/)

Formed in 2003, the Sierra Buttes Trail Stewardship is a volunteer-driven 501c3 nonprofit dedicated to the maintenance and enhancement of trail systems in the Lost Sierra, a region that offers natural beauty, remote accessibility and diverse multi-use recreational opportunities. Our professional trail crew helps create and rebuild trails that are enjoyable for all user types: hikers, cyclists, dirt bikers, equestrians and anglers.

SBTS employs around 37 full-time and seasonal employees, most of which are Sierra and Plumas County residents, working on [trail projects](https://copper-alligator-9yh3.squarespace.com/trail-projects) across the region in partnership with the U.S. Forest Service. In addition to staffing a paid crew, SBTS has to-date donated 140,000 hours of labor through its dedicated volunteers. Together, we have maintained more than 3,000 miles of  shared-use trails and built 220+ miles of new trails.

## What We've Accomplished Since 2003

# 227

**Miles of New Trail Built**

# 3,082

**Miles of Trail Maintained to Specification**

# 3

**Pro Trail Crews in 2026**

# 40

**Employees in 2025**

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/681e46c994b3ba7455d102a0/c947e782-fd27-4010-b4f5-e14c759531af/sierra-buttes-trail-stewardship-hiking.jpg)

### “What makes Sierra Buttes different? The fact that they can drum up volunteers when they need them, at a moment’s notice,” said Rick Stock, a retired teacher at the Feather River College in Quincy. Stock taught recreation classes and was on the board of Sierra Buttes Trail Stewardship for four years. “People drive up from the bay or Sac to be part of some volunteer event. I don’t want to say it’s unheard of, but Sierra Buttes has a way to do it that’s more prolific than others I would say.”

— SF Gate

### Withstanding The Test of Time

While these trails see more than **200,000** visitors per year, they continue to maintain a level “A” standing, due to the hard work of SBTS staff and volunteers. In a perfect world, the Forest Service would be able to attend to all of these system trails (wilderness, roadless, recreation) as part of ongoing resource management. And that’s where SBTS and our family – our hardworking volunteers and members – come in, partnering with [land managers](https://copper-alligator-9yh3.squarespace.com/partner-with-us) to make dirt magic happen.

Trail bed armoring, grade reversals, drainage reconstruction, and grade reductions are all techniques employed for longevity and erosion control. By minimizing use impact through trail maintenance while not restricting access, the historic and recreational value of these trails has been maintained. And we’ve worked on everything from garden-variety singletrack, to Pacific Crest Trail in wilderness areas, to ADA-compliant paths, to multiple-use flow trails.

### Making Our Effort Count

[Event](http://static1.squarespace.com/static/681e46c994b3ba7455d102a0/681e8b1b538ff676414ffac0/681e8b5a538ff67641500a39/1746832218987/?format=original) income, [membership](http://static1.squarespace.com/static/681e46c994b3ba7455d102a0/681e8b1b538ff676414ffac0/681e8b5b538ff67641500a3c/1746832219014/?format=original), grants (county, state, federal, private), donations, and our bike shop [Yuba Expeditions](https://copper-alligator-9yh3.squarespace.com/yuba-expeditions) in Quincy go directly to trail maintenance and development in the [Lost Sierra](https://copper-alligator-9yh3.squarespace.com/the-lost-sierra). Donations are multiplied by over 500 percent through organized volunteer labor and in-kind contributions. And we have even helped other trail user organizations in South Lake Tahoe, Santa Cruz, the Sacramento Valley and the Sierra foothills with planning, construction and trail improvements. **View our 2025 Annual Report** to learn about our economic impact, partnerships and fundraising we achieved to support Lost Sierra communities.

![Black and white photograph of mountainous terrain with rocky peaks and a forested foreground. Overlaid text reads: "Established 2003 Our mission: Building sustainable recreation-based communities through stewardship, job creation and world-class events. Providing quality outdoor experiences through trail construction and maintenance in the Lost Sierra."](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/681e46c994b3ba7455d102a0/6c72c333-8514-41de-9383-01b078cc1669/SBTS-presentation-1.png)

Click to view the 2025 Annual Report

### The SBTS Family

Our organization is a shining example of what a small group of dedicated, passionate people can do. We are hikers, mountain bikers, motorcycle riders, equestrians and anglers playing in the outdoors. We are the descendants of native tribes and fourth-generation miners. We are the ones with chainsaws in backpacks as the snow melts, doing maintenance and clearing away winter's deadfall. We are the people caring for something very special, and keeping it special for our friends, families, and generations to come. And we have fun too! [Join us](http://static1.squarespace.com/static/681e46c994b3ba7455d102a0/681e8b1b538ff676414ffac0/681e8b5b538ff67641500a3c/1746832219014/?format=original) – become a member, dedicate your time at one of our [Volunteer Epic weekends](https://sierratrails.org/events) and/or [race events](http://static1.squarespace.com/static/681e46c994b3ba7455d102a0/681e8b1b538ff676414ffac0/681e8b5a538ff67641500a39/1746832218987/?format=original), and make a difference!

![Sierra Buttes Trail Stewardship staff](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/681e46c994b3ba7455d102a0/c58ddb53-5f65-4826-bac2-fd4f823ec4b1/sbts-staff-photo-2025-web.jpg)

### GENERAL INFORMATION

*   What is The One Motorcycle Show Portland?
    
    For 17 years, The One Motorcycle Show has been celebrating motorcycles, art, and community. Held annually at Portland’s historic Zidell Yards, it brings together custom bikes from around the globe, moto-inspired art, cars, helmets, live music, vendors, demos, and loads of FUN. There’s something for everyone. 2026 TICKETS LIVE DEC 1ST!!
    
*   When is The One Motorcycle Show Portland?
    
    Year 17 of The One Motorcycle Show is happening Friday, May 1st - Sunday, May 2nd, 2026.
    
    **Portland Show Hours**
    
    5/1/2026: 9 AM - 10 PM
    
    5/2/2026: 9 AM - 10 PM
    
    5/3/2026: 9 AM - 3 PM
    
    **_Online ticket sales end April 30th at 11:59 PM! General Admission available at the door (prices increase). Weekend & Day Passes are available online only._**
    
*   Where is The One Motorcycle Show Portland?
    
    It’s happening once again at the historic [**Zidell Yards - 3121 S Moody Ave, Portland, Oregon 97239**.](https://www.the1moto.com/venue) Our fifth year at this rad venue. Don’t miss it!
    
    **_Online ticket sales end April 30th at 11:59 PM! General Admission available at the door (prices increase). Weekend & Day Passes are available online only._**
    
*   How can I get tickets to The One Motorcycle Show?
    
    Tickets to The One Motorcycle Show are available for purchase [**HERE**](https://www.tixr.com/groups/1moto/events/the-one-motorcycle-show-portland-166660).
    
    **_Online ticket sales end April 30th at 11:59 PM! General Admission available at the door (prices increase). Weekend & Day Passes are available online only._**
    
*   Is The One Motorcycle Show Portland family-friendly?
    
    Heck yeah! The show’s open to all ages and fun for the whole fam. Kids 10 and under get in free with an adult. Daytime’s great for families, but everyone’s welcome anytime during the event!
    
    **_Online ticket sales end April 30th at 11:59 PM! General Admission available at the door (prices increase). Weekend & Day Passes are available online only._**
    
*   Are pets allowed at the show?
    
    Pets, with the exception of service animals, are generally not allowed inside the event venue due to safety and space considerations.
    
*   Will there be food and drinks available at the show?
    
    You bet! We’ve got food vendors serving up tasty eats and plenty of drink options to keep you fueled all day. Wanna join the lineup? Click [**HERE**](https://www.the1moto.com/get-involved) to apply to be a vendor at the PORTLAND show! Or reach out to [**vendors@theonemoto.com**](mailto:vendors@theonemoto.com).
    
*   Are there accommodations nearby for out-of-town visitors?
    
    There are lots of hotels, motels, and Airbnb spots near the venue, but they fill up quick so book early! Check [**HERE**](https://www.the1moto.com/hotels) for all the latest & preferred hotel recommendations.
    
*   Is there parking available at the event?
    
    Parking is limited, so we recommend riding your bike, carpooling, or using public transit when you can. Motorcycle parking is free, first-come, first-served, and right near the main entrance.
    
*   Is the venue ADA accessible?
    
    Yes, although it is not an ideal space for wheelchairs as there is not any sidewalk. There are ramps to all elevated spaces within the venue, but due to the nature of the industrial building and the outdoor areas around it, please be aware that there are many areas at the event venue with uneven ground.
    
*   Do you have ADA / handicap parking available?
    
    Limited accessible parking options are available on site near the main show entrance, first come first serve. Our parking attendants will help get you there. We will also have ADA-compliant restrooms available.
    
*   Are there any prohibited items?
    
    **Prohibited Items**
    
    NO WEAPONS OF ANY KIND – Including Firearms, Pocket Knives, Pepper Spray, tasers, etc.
    
    These items will be confiscated via Local Authorities and Security. 
    
    ❌ Backpacks, Purses, or Bags larger than 14″ x 14″ 
    
    ❌ Illegal Substances, Drugs or Drug Paraphernalia
    
    ❌ Unsealed Over the Counter Medications or Vitamins
    
    ❌ Animals (except service animals)
    
    ❌ Outside alcohol
    
    ❌ Fireworks, open fires, flammable products, projectiles, or explosives
    
    ❌ Drones or Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs).
    
    ❌ Glass of any kind
    
    ❌ Lasers or pointer devices
    
    ❌ Tactical Gear, Walkie Talkies, etc.
    
    ❌ Items deemed as posing a threat to the safe enjoyment of the One Motorcycle Show by management.
    
    Please check out our [Community Code of Conduct](https://www.the1moto.com/code-of-conduct) for more info.
    

### SUBMISSIONS

*   How can I submit my build to be in the show?
    
    Got a custom bike you’re ready to show off? The One Motorcycle Show wants to see it! Click [**HERE**](https://www.the1moto.com/get-involved) for all the details on how to submit your ride.
    
*   When will I hear back about my bike being accepted or not?
    
    Accepted builds will know before or by March 7th, 2026, via email. Once accepted, we'll send you a physical invite via the ol' postman (in the mail) by April 1st, 2026.
    
*   How can I submit my art?
    
    Wanna get your art in the mix? Click [**HERE**](https://www.the1moto.com/get-involved) to learn more about getting involved.
    
*   How can I apply to be a vendor?
    
    Fresh oysters? Cool wares? Moto Gear? We’re into it. Locals get dibs. Check out how to get involved [**HERE**](https://www.the1moto.com/get-involved).
    
*   How can I participate in the 21 Helmets showcase?
    
    Shoot an email over to [**thor@theonemoto.com**](mailto:thor@theonemoto.com) for more info!
    
*   How can I submit my band?
    
    Thanks for your interest! Band submissions aren’t currently open, but if you think your band should be on our radar, drop a line to **mahala@theonemoto.com**.
    
*   Is photography allowed at The One Motorcycle Show?
    
    Yes, general photography is allowed, but please be mindful of others while snapping photos. By attending The One Motorcycle Show, you agree to being photographed, filmed, or recorded. Official photographers and media can apply for a press badge to access exclusive events. Click [**HERE**](https://www.the1moto.com/media) for more info.
    
*   How can I apply for a media pass?
    
    Interested in covering the show? Media credentials are limited. Apply [**HERE**](https://www.the1moto.com/get-involved) to be considered! Questions? Email [**media@theonemoto.com**](mailto:media@theonemoto.com?).
    
*   How can I apply to volunteer at the show?
    
    Click [**HERE**](https://www.the1moto.com/get-involved) for more info!
    

### SHOW PROGRAM

*   Is there an event schedule for the show?
    
    Yep! Check it out above! Keep checking back for the latest info & updates!
    
*   Will there be any offsite events, parties or racing?
    
    Check out the full weekend schedule for off-site after parties you can’t miss! Interested in teaming up for a good time? Hit up **marian@theonemoto.com**.
    
*   Will there be a bike showcase?
    
    Yup!! Custom bikes from all over the world. It’s what The One’s all about.
    
*   What bands are performing?
    
    We’ve got a killer lineup brewing! Check back soon!
    
*   Will there be demos?
    
    Of course! Demos are a staple. We’ll share more info on what’s lined up closer to the show.
    
*   What activities will be at the show?
    
    Bikes, bands, cars, art, food, stunts, vendors... you name it. The One Motorcycle Show is a wheelie wonderland.
    
*   Are there activities for kids?
    
    Yep! Bring the whole fam. There’s something for everyone (and kids 10 and under are free when accompanied with an adult!). We have plenty of fun for the whole family!
    
*   What kind of vendors will be there?
    
    From moto gear to vintage fashion, jewelry, art, and tasty eats, our vendors cover it all.
    
*   Will there be food and drinks available?
    
    Plenty! We’ve got food trucks, drinks, and all the good stuff to keep you fueled for the day.
    
*   Is there a map of the venue?
    
    Check it out above! Keep checking back for the latest info!
    
*   Tips for The One Motorcycle Show first-timers?
    
    Get ready for a good time! Wear comfy shoes, bring a charged phone for pics, and don’t rush… there’s A LOT to see. Arrive early, grab your tickets online to save a few bucks, and snag a [**Weekend Pass**](https://www.tixr.com/groups/1moto) so you don’t miss a single drop of the fun!
    
    **_Online ticket sales end April 30th at 11:59 PM! General Admission available at the door (prices increase). Weekend & Day Passes are available online only._**
    
*   Will there be The One Motorcycle merch for sale at the show?
    
    Oh yeah—plenty of it! Grab some world-famous One Moto gear, posters, hats and maybe even a few surprises you won’t find anywhere else! In the meantime, check out our online merch shop [**HERE**](https://the1moto.com/shop) for the latest drops!
    
    **_Online ticket sales end May 1st at 11:59 PM! General Admission available at the door (prices increase). Weekend & Day Passes are available online only._**
    

### TICKETS

*   How can I attend The One Motorcycle Show?
    
    Tickets for The One Motorcycle Show are available [HERE](https://www.tixr.com/groups/1moto). Grab yours early—this event sells out fast! Prices go up at the door, so save by purchasing in advance. Day and Weekend Passes available online only.
    
*   Can I get a refund?
    
    Refunds are available until the day of the show. For assistance with refunds, please send an email to [**support@tixr.com**](mailto:support@tixr.com?). They will be able to assist you with the refund process.
    
*   Can I change the name on my ticket?
    
    Unfortunately, name changes on tickets are not allowed at this time. 
    
*   Can I transfer my ticket to another person?
    
    Currently, ticket transfers to another individual are not permitted.
    
*   Can I resell my ticket?
    
    We do not support the resale of tickets.
    

### ONLINE SHOP

#### Refund Policy

*   What is your policy on refunds, returns, and exchanges?
    
    We accept returns within 30 days after delivery if the item is unused and in its original condition. We will refund the full order amount, minus the shipping costs for the return. In case your order arrives damaged, please contact us at info@theonemoto.com with your order number and a photo of the item's condition for a case-by-case assessment.
    
*   Are there any items that cannot be returned or exchanged?
    
    Products on sale are not eligible for return or exchange.
    
*   Who covers the return shipping costs?
    
    The buyer is responsible for return shipping costs. Original shipping fees are non-refundable.
    
*   How long does it take to process a refund?
    
    Refunds may take 2-7 days to process after we receive and approve the return, depending on your payment method and credit card company.
    

#### Shipping

*   How long does it take to process and ship my order?
    
    All orders are processed within 2 to 5 business days, excluding weekends and holidays. After your order is confirmed, you will receive a shipping notification. Delivery times vary but typically take 5-10 business days, depending on your location.
    
*   What are the shipping rates and how are they calculated?
    
    We offer free shipping for orders over $50. For orders under $50, shipping charges are calculated and displayed at checkout based on your order size and shipping destination.
    
*   How can I track the status of my order?
    
    Once your order has shipped, you will receive an email with a tracking number. You can use this number to check the status of your delivery. Please allow 48 hours for the tracking information to become available.
    
*   Do you offer a local pick-up option?
    
    Yes! You can pick up your order at One Moto Cafe, 1642 NE Sandy Blvd., Portland, OR 97232, daily from 7 AM to 3 PM. Just select local pick-up at checkout, and we’ll email you when it’s ready—usually within 2 to 5 business days. Questions about local pick-up? Email info@theonemoto.com.

# Portland Zine Symposium

**The Portland Zine Symposium (PZS)** is an organization that hosts, among other events, a yearly free conference and zine social exploring facets of independent publishing and DIY culture. This event has been held in Portland, Oregon every summer since 2001 and hosts over 150 zinesters from around the world each year, as well as many free workshops, panels, and discussions.

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5db36411537a5149d59dc210/611966f4-9d1f-4dcc-b84c-8cd4f7eab0a2/pzs.jpeg)

### Mission Statement

**The Portland Zine Symposium (PZS)** aims to build community between creators of independent publications in Portland, OR and beyond. PZS events create space for artists to share their work while exchanging skills and knowledge related to zine culture, creative expression, and self-publishing in an accessible, non-commercial environment.  PZS strives to amplify the voices of underrepresented communities, and promote equitable conditions for Portland’s creative community to thrive.

### PZS Organizers

**The Portland Zine Symposium is run by volunteer organizers!** Below are just a few of the folks helping organize the Portland Zine Symposium:

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5db36411537a5149d59dc210/5dcfe9d3-4800-42b3-a143-678d904b1174/me+at+souwester+%3C3.jpg)

Emily Moroz (she/her/they) is a cartoonist, illustrator, gay outdoorslady and member of the Sound Grounds Wreckin’ Cru. Find more at [moreohs.com](http://www.moreohs.com/) and on IG [@moreohs.art.](http://www.instagram.com/moreohs.art)

![Person with cool cat-eye glasses and green/yellow hair. They're wearing a pink-ish beret and the background looks like comics and art prints!](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5db36411537a5149d59dc210/075bc33f-c0ae-4cfb-88df-4deb3e11ffda/20240324_185327.jpg)

#### Wren McSherry

Wren is 27 years old wringing and slinging comics for the people. They like cats, tea, film, and ranting about 70s manga. You can find them on insta [@crowsden](https://www.instagram.com/crowsden/).

![A brown haired person with a beard plus mustache combo wearing some cool black glasses.](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5db36411537a5149d59dc210/6f073315-1eb1-4a98-b821-031a754b4329/rainer.jpg)

#### Rainer Kannenstine

Rainer Kannenstine (He/Him) is a Portland based cartoonist focusing on the weird and wonderful. You can find his work [@rfkannen](https://www.instagram.com/rfkannen/) everywhere with handles.

![A person with blue eyes and a light beard & mustache wearing cool thin-rimmed glasses and looking past the camera.](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5db36411537a5149d59dc210/1582081468352-ZK81DT2QQ496BETUK39U/emlyn.jpg)

Emlyn Thompson is an out-of-practice artist and lifelong monster enthusiast. He doesn't really have an online presence, but he's working to change that.

![A person with short brown hair, blue eyes, and a light beard. They're wearing a kippah on their head and leaning in to smell a rose. The background is the International Rose Test Garden with flowers and grass!](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5db36411537a5149d59dc210/b566f3ba-e625-43ea-8fee-ed1ba540fe99/PXL_20230613_195135717.MP.jpg)

#### CJ Alicandro

CJ Alicandro (they/them) is a self-proclaimed patron of the arts. Proudly queer Jew, karaoke enthusiast, union supporter, and all-around busy body.

![A person with long dark hair smiling at the camera. They're wearing some neat thicker-rimmed glasses in maybe a tortoise shell style.](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5db36411537a5149d59dc210/1619663379336-OW2FFL532O18Y8SQ8Y4A/BB_Profile_02.jpg)

BB Andersson is a cartoonist,  
zinester, designer, and multimedia artist. Find their work at [bbandersson.com](https://bbandersson.com/) and on instagram [@bbandersson](http://www.instagram.com/bbandersson)

![Person with long light brown hair and blue/green eyes wearing a purple/blue/pink hat with little poof balls on it. The hat covers their chin too like it's part scarf! Emma (she/they) is a graphic designer & zinester. She can be found gardening, working on [LURCH Zine](https://www.instagram.com/lurchzine/), or at a show. See more of Emma’s work at [@emmawisegnome.](https://www.instagram.com/emmawisegnome/)

## FAQ

よくあるご質問

– 競技観戦上のルールについて

Q.応援・観戦のマナーについて

A.会場付近での路上飲酒・喫煙や、たむろ行為は禁止です。ルールとマナーを守ったうえで、お楽しみ下さい。

Q.選手・出演者へプレゼントを渡すことはできますか?

A.感染拡大防止策の一環として、選手・出演者へのプレゼントの持ち込みは禁止いたします。

– チケットに関して

Q.チケットの販売はありますか？

A.入場無料ですので、チケット等の販売はございません。

Q.再入場は可能ですか？

A.再入場は可能です。

– 会場内について

Q.当日の服装は？

A.野外のため突然の天候の変化もございます。昼と夜の気温差も考慮いただき、調節可能な服装でご来場ください。

Q.雨天・強風の場合はどうなりますか？

A.当日の天気予報をもとに、中止あるいは遅延の判断をいたします。随時オフィシャルサイト、SNSをご確認ください。

Q.会場は禁煙ですか？

A.指定の喫煙所がございます。場所とマナーをお守りいただき、ご利用ください。

Q.乳幼児の飲食物の持ち込みはできますか？

A.持ち込み可能です。

Q.ベビーカーの持ち込みは可能ですか？

A.持ち込み可能となります。

Q.ペットと一緒に入場することができますか？

A.可能です。エリアによってペットの入場が不可の場合がございます。

Q.カメラ撮影はできますか？

A.競技エリアのカメラ撮影は可能です。なお、三脚等の機材を使用した撮影は他のお客様のご迷惑となりますのでご遠慮ください。

Q.レジャーシートやタープ、折りたたみ椅子などは使用できますか？

A.レジャーシート、椅子、タープ、パラソル等持ち込みできません。会場内に設置するベンチ等を譲り合ってご利用下さい。

Q.持ち込み禁止のものはありますか？

A.テント、ビン、クーラーボックス、花火、爆竹等の危険物、セルフィースティック、ペンライト、レーザーポインター等、周囲のお客様のご迷惑になる物に関してもお持込みできません。

– 物販について

Q.会場での販売はありますか?

A.販売いたします。会場内のマーケットプレイスにてフード・ドリンクなどを販売いたします。

\- ご来場方法について

Q.手荷物検査はありますか？

A.入場の際、手荷物検査はございませんが不審物・危険物等の持ち込みは禁止です。不審物の持ち込みを発見次第、いかなる場合であっても警察に通報させて頂きます。

Q.当日車での来場は可能ですか？ 駐車場はありますか？

A.お車でご来場されるお客様は横浜赤レンガ倉庫周辺の駐車場が大変混雑することが予想されますので予めご了承ください。ご来場されるお客様はなるべく公共交通機関をご利用ください。

Q.当日自転車での来場は可能ですか？ 駐輪場はありますか？

A.公共の駐輪場はございますが、多くの方の来場が予想され、駐輪スペースがないことも考えられますので公共交通機関のご利用をお願いいたします。また、近隣の皆様のご迷惑となりますので、会場周辺等への路上駐輪等は絶対に行わないでください。

Q.当日スケートボードやBMXでの来場は可能ですか？

A.横浜赤レンガ倉庫エリアはスケートボードやBMXの乗り入れは禁止となっています。当イベントは特別な許可を得て開催しており、許可されているエリア以外での乗り入れはご遠慮ください。

## ABOUT

YUSFについて

### ![日本最大級アーバンスポーツの祭典](//yusf.jp/wp-content/themes/yusf/images/largest-title.svg) ![日本最大級アーバンスポーツの祭典](//yusf.jp/wp-content/themes/yusf/images/largest-title_sp.svg)

スポーツという枠だけに収まらず  
「音楽・ファッション・アート」などストリートカルチャーと密接に結びついているアーバンスポーツ。  
野球やサッカーといったスポーツが盛んな街、横浜。  
この街を舞台に、アーバンスポーツが持つ魅力の全てを凝縮したフェスティバルを開催します。  
これからを担う新しい世代と共に、アーバンスポーツが横浜の街に  
ライフスタイルとして根付いていく事を目指します。

![](https://yusf.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/bg_mv-1024x614.png?auto=compress,format&lossless=0)

「競技としてのプロスポーツとバックボーンにあるストリートカルチャーの魅力が融合したアーバンスポーツのエンターテインメントイベント『YOKOHAMA URBAN SPORTS FESTIVAL』が、来たる10月17日（土）・18日（日）の2日間、横浜赤レンガ倉庫にて開催されます。  
 本イベントは、アーバンスポーツ競技と、そのスポーツの原点とも言えるストリートカルチャーが一堂に会し、「観る・体験する・楽しむ」要素が満載のスポーツフェスティバルであり、昨年度は約7万人を動員しました。  
 5回目の開催となる今年は、スケートボード、ブレイキン、BMXフラットランド、ダブルダッチ、パルクール、パルオニ、3X3、フリースタイルフットボールの全8種目に、国内外で活躍する選手の登場が予定されております。さらに、今年のブレイキン種目では、日本ダンススポーツ連盟主催の「JAPAN OPEN 2026」の開催が決定し、日本各地から集結する選手によるハイレベルなダンスバトルにも注目です。その他、大人から子どもまでアーバンスポーツを気軽にチャレンジできる体験会や、ファッションやアイテムが勢揃いのストリートカルチャーマーケット、そして昨年に引き続き同時開催されるアメリカンフードフェス『ALL AMERICAN FOOD FESTIVAL ’26』など、2日間に収まりきらない盛りだくさんの企画をご用意して皆様のご来場をお待ちしております。」

フラグシップ商品のGRAVELKINGは国内・海外の大人気のタイヤです。近年ではグラベル文化を広めるため各地のイベントを応援しています。

vivobarefoot（ビボベアフット）は、足が本来もつ機能や筋力を取り戻すことで、姿勢、バランス、動き､メンタルなど、幅広い面でポジティブな変化をもたらしてくれるシューズです。ブースでは試着や展示販売などを行います。

[![](https://nisekogravel.com/sys/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/partner_ono.jpg)](https://onosapporo.jp/) [有限会社サイクル小野サッポロ](https://onosapporo.jp/)

自転車は「使い捨てのもの」ではなく、「生活の中で特別な楽しい乗り物」です。　はじめての一台から、とっておきの一台まで、当店は、自転車との素敵な出会いをお手伝いします。

[![](https://nisekogravel.com/sys/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/partner_LAVAGGIO.jpg)](https://coubic.com/lavaggio/4083173) [LAVAGGIO](https://coubic.com/lavaggio/4083173)

ラバッジョは今年もニセコグラベルで「洗車」と「配送」のサポートを行います。今年の洗車は普段皆さんが実現できないところまで踏み込んだ研磨作業付き、そして配送は帰りの片道パックもご用意しております。愛車とあなたがニセコグラベルを笑顔で締めくくれるようにラバッジョがサポートします。

[![](https://nisekogravel.com/sys/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/partner_NAMBA.jpg)](https://namba.ngo/) [NAMBA](https://namba.ngo/)

ニセコエリアマウンテンバイク協会（NAMBA）は、北海道ニセコを拠点とするNPO法人です。地域唯一のMTB協会として、ボランティア主導で持続可能なトレイル整備を行い、スキー場や土地所有者、企業と連携。ライダーの声を代弁し、マウンテンバイク文化を広め、ニセコを世界に誇れるMTBデスティネーションへと導いています。

[![](https://nisekogravel.com/sys/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/partner_FineProduce.jpg)](http://fine-produce.com/) [Fine Produce](http://fine-produce.com/)

日常生活からスポーツまで快適にするインソール体験会を行います。足圧測定でバランスチェックしてみてください。

[![](https://nisekogravel.com/sys/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/partner_UPstudio.jpg)](https://www.instagram.com/up_studio2023) [UP STUDIO](https://www.instagram.com/up_studio2023)

UP STUDIOは、ジャンル問わず、いろいろなイベントでLIVEプリントをしております！普段は、シルクスクリーンプリントで、各イベント、お祭り、スポーツチーム、各企業様のユニフォーム、ノベルティーやオリジナルグッズをデザインから手掛けております。ニセコグラベルでは、参加記念品Tシャツ制作、イベント当日はその日限定のオリジナルTシャツを会場でLIVEプリントいたします！

[![](https://nisekogravel.com/sys/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/partner_panaracer_photo.jpg)](https://panaracer.com/)

[![](https://nisekogravel.com/sys/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/partner_panaracer_logo.png)](https://panaracer.com/)

## General

### General FAQ’s

#### What Is Sea Otter?

**Sea Otter Australia** is a multi-day Cycling Festival held in Batemans Bay and Mogo Trails on the NSW South Coast. The event is organised by Rocky Trail Entertainment, one of the country’s major private mountain bike event promoters.  
  
In a nutshell, Sea Otter Australia is the Southern Hemisphere’s only edition of the iconic Sea Otter cycling festival, established in California’s Monterey over 30 years ago. With Girona in Spain, Sea Otter Europe, our Festival is one of just two licensed global events. Launched in Batemans Bay and Mogo Trails, NSW, it’s a multi-day celebration of all things bike, blending world-class racing across disciplines (enduro, XC, gravel, e-bikes and more) with an expansive expo featuring the latest bikes, gear, demos, and deals.  
  
Kicking off with a two-day [Sea Otter Summit](https://seaotter.au/summit/), the event brings together leaders in trail tourism, the bike industry, and government to shape the future of cycling in Australia. Then the action shifts to the [multi-day festival](https://seaotter.au/whats-on/)— packed with racing, riding, and family-friendly activities—set against the backdrop of the newly built Mogo Trails, 125 km of purpose-built trails on Yuin Country.  
  
Sea Otter Australia is more than a festival—it’s a hub for connection, innovation, and the growth of cycling culture in Australia.

#### When Is It On?

Sea Otter Australia kicks off with the 2 day Summit followed by the Main Festival & Expo on 23-25 October.

#### Where is Sea Otter Australia being held?

Sea Otter Australia is launched in Batemans Bay on the South Coast of NSW, Australia. The Event Hub and Expo – and the heart of all the action – is based right in town at the Hanging Rock Sports Precinct; all races and rides start from here. The Event Hub is a short ride to one of the main network entries to Mogo Trails, which will host the races and Gravel Fondo.

#### Who should come to Sea Otter

**Sea Otter Australia is for everyone who loves bikes—whether you ride, race, work in the industry, or just want to soak up the atmosphere.** It’s perfect for mountain bikers, gravel grinders, roadies, e-bike enthusiasts, families, and kids discovering the joy of cycling. Racers can test themselves across a huge range of disciplines, while fans and first-timers can demo new gear, explore the expo, and enjoy a festival vibe with food, music, and activities for all ages. [See What’s On](https://seaotter.au/whats-on/)!

#### About Inclusivity

Sea Otter is for everyone. Our vision is to create the most immersive mountain bike and cycling celebration Australia has ever seen, igniting a passion for two-wheeled adventures in everyone.  
Our organisers from Rocky Trail Entertainment are dedicated to fostering a vibrant and welcoming community for all who share a passion for cycling. We believe that the thrill of the ride and the spirit of competition should be accessible to everyone.  
With a commitment to inclusion, equity, and diversity, we strive to create environments at all our events that celebrate the unique talents, backgrounds, and perspectives of every individual.  
We offer non-binary categories at our events, ensuring that participants of all gender identities find their place at our start lines.  
We have also been working with the adaptive riding community and our industry partners to customise and adapt races and tracks so that we can provide a suitable experience offer to adaptive riders.  
With 40+ cycling events along the East Coast, we recognise our opportunity and responsibility to lead by example. We are continuously listening, learning, and implementing changes to make a lasting and meaningful impact for our riders, volunteers, partners, and the entire endurance cycling community. Our goal is for everyone to feel welcomed, respected, supported, and valued, moving forward to the finish line together.

#### About Sustainability and Accessibility

Rocky Trail Entertainment respects and supports the pleasures of mountain biking and related self-reliant outdoor activities. As such we advocate that all of us have a big responsibility to protect and preserve the natural landscape for the enjoyment of future generations.  
At the core of all our efforts to put together the annual racing calendar is, and will always be, the trails. We work with property managers and organisations, local councils and clubs and our goal is to deliver a versatile selection of terrain, regions and mountain bike trails, including adaptive trails. We include many regional trail networks as this gives more mountain bikers the chance to race on their local trails. It also promotes less frequented trail networks to visiting riders and encourages them to discover new trails.  
Rocky Trail Entertainment understands the importance that our product offering is accessible to people of all abilities. The nature of the competitive activities that Rocky Trail Entertainment provides on off-road trails, will be limited for people with a disability. However, we want to be as accommodating for staff and guests of all abilities fosters diversity and acceptance, which resonates through to employee and customer satisfaction.  
We have been working with the adaptive riding community and our industry partners to customise and adapt races and tracks so that we can provide a suitable experience offer to adaptive riders.  
  
Full Sustainability and Accessibility Statement is available via [https://rockytrailentertainment.com/about/sustainability-accessibility-policy/](https://rockytrailentertainment.com/about/sustainability-accessibility-policy/)

#### How we care about the Environment

**Tread Softly, Ride Hard: Our Shared Commitment to the Trails**  
When we line up at the start gates or walk the expo floor at Hanging Rock and the Mogo Trails this October, we are occupying some of the most spectacular natural terrain in regional New South Wales. As riders, parents, and industry crews, we all share a foundational responsibility to protect the land that serves as our playground. For Sea Otter Australia 2026, sustainability isn’t an afterthought or a corporate checkbox—it is a live operational framework built into every square meter of the festival footprint.  
  
To back this up, all Rocky Trail events including Sea Otter Australia are certified by [Ecotourism Australia and are operating with integrated ECO Certification standards](https://rockytrailentertainment.com/about/ecotourism-certification/) across the entire event delivery structure. This means our environmental policy aligns with verified ecological requirements, ensuring our presence leaves no long-term footprint on the native landscape. From trail care protocols to resource conservation, we are setting a clear benchmark for what a major international cycling festival can achieve. By committing to Ecotourism Australia Nature Certification our business joins fellow exemplary operators in terms of sustainability and provision of authentic, high-quality nature-based tourism experiences. The ECO Certification logo means that with Rocky Trail our riders and supporters are guaranteed to be part of a genuine and authentic trail-based nature experience that looks after the environment. The ECO Certification program assures that our certified events are backed by a commitment to sustainable practices and provide high quality nature-based tourism experiences.  
  
**Real Action on Waste: Eurobodalla Shire Council**  
We have teamed up with the Eurobodalla Shire Council Sustainability Team to completely re-engineer our waste management program. Instead of relying on generic public bins, the council team is helping us implement colour-coded, clearly labelled waste sorting stations across the entire festival hub.  
They will also be assisting us with comprehensive on-site waste audits to measure exact recycling rates and identify areas for improvement. For our exhibitors and B2B partners, we are actively pushing a strict waste-reduction policy in the trade zones. We are asking all brands to minimise packaging materials before they arrive and to eliminate short-lived promotional giveaways entirely.  
  
**Joining the Global Movement: Trash Free Trails**  
Sea Otter Australia 2026 is officially a Trash Free Trails (TFT) approved event. We are partnering with the local TFT Australia team to foster a strict “Leave It Better” culture across every single race and demo stage. The TFT crew will be active on the ground with their custom ‘bin-bike’ to manage pre- and post-race course sweeps, ensuring no stray litter remains in the bush.  
Our shared target with TFT is a roadmap toward a true Zero Trace Race. One of our biggest collective targets this year is eliminating the classic “gel end” – those tiny, jagged silver foil tear-offs from energy gel packets that clog up singletrack and endanger local wildlife. We are asking every competitor to tuck those tear-offs safely inside their sleeves or pockets, or switch to modern leash-style packaging. Learn more at [TrashFreeTrails.au](http://trashfreetrails.au/)  
  
**What We Ask of the Sea Otter Community**  
Whether you are aiming for a podium, racing or riding with mates, exhibiting in the hub, or cheering on the crowds, you play a direct role in this plan. We ask that you bring reusable bottles and cups, utilise the free water refill stations, and strictly sort your rubbish at the designated bays.  
  
Let’s make sure the only things we leave behind on the Mogo Trails are tyre marks and good memories.

## Muc-Off Ottercross

### Muc-Off Ottercross FAQ’s

#### How long is the course?

The course will be approximately 2km including a 300m beach section

#### Where is the start & finish?

The start and finish is right in the heart of the main event center at Hanging Rock.

#### Do we ride on the beach?

Yes there is a 3-400 meter section along the beach!

Tyre Width

#### What’s the maximum tyre width for A Grade?

A Grade enforces the UCI standard of 33mm maximum measured width.

#### Can I run wider tyres in B Grade?

Yes, B Grade allows up to 42mm to accommodate stock gravel bikes.

#### Is there a tyre width limit for C Grade, Juniors or Sub Juniors?

No, these categories have no tyre restriction. Ride what you have.

Bike

#### What bikes are allowed in A Grade?

Strictly drop-bar cyclocross or gravel bikes, to maintain the traditional CX spirit and UCI standard.

#### Can I ride a mountain bike in B Grade?

Yes, mountain bikes are allowed in B Grade, though drop bars are encouraged.

#### What bikes are allowed in C Grade, Juniors and Sub Juniors?

Any safe bicycle, including mountain bikes, flat-bar gravel bikes, and older road bikes with suitable tyres. It’s a run-what-you-brung spirit.

The Pits

#### Where can I get technical assistance during the race?

Only within the designated Technical Zone (the Pit). Self-sufficiency is required everywhere else on the course.

#### Where is the Pit located?

It’s a two-sided pit with double entry/exit, positioned at approximately the 1.2km mark and again at the 2km mark of a 2.5km lap.

#### What kind of assistance can I get in the Pit?

Hand-ups, tools, spare parts and full bike changes are all permitted within the Technical Zone.

#### Can someone hand me a spare part or tool outside the Pit?

No, assistance from non-competitors is not allowed anywhere else on the course.

#### Can I stage a spare bike?

A and B Grade riders may stage one spare bike in the Pit. C Grade riders may also stage one spare bike, or use a mountain bike as their primary.

#### What happens if my bike breaks down away from the Pit?

If the mechanical failure makes the bike unrideable, you must carry or run with it to the Pit to receive assistance.

#### Can I take a gel or drink from a spectator on course?

No, feeding and hand-ups are not permitted outside the Technical Zone. Any wrappers or bottles must be carried by you and disposed of responsibly.

#### What about beer hand-ups?

In keeping with the spirit of Ottercross, beer hand-ups will be ignored.
